required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: runner_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner.

title: Delete a team
description: Deletes a team (and any child teams) from an organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization's unique identifier (case-insensitive).

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The team's URL-friendly slug.

title: Delete a thread subscription
description: Call this to mute a specific notification thread by deleting the user's subscription; notifications may still occur if the user is @mentioned, comments, or due to repository watch settings.

required.name: thread_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the notification thread. This ID is obtained from other API calls, such as when listing notifications (e.g., via the `GET /notifications` endpoint). Ensure this ID refers to an active thread to which the user is currently subscribed.

title: Delete an autolink reference from a repository
description: Deletes a specific autolink reference (which automatically links external resource IDs like JIRA-123 to URLs) from the specified repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This is not case-sensitive.

required.name: autolink_id
required.description: The unique numerical identifier of the autolink reference to be deleted.

title: Delete a workflow run
description: Deletes a specific workflow run from a repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run.

title: Delete branch protection
description: Removes all protection rules from a specific branch in a GitHub repository; the branch must currently have protection rules enabled.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. Not case sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch. Wildcard characters are not supported for this REST API endpoint; use the GitHub GraphQL API for wildcard support.

title: Delete a code scanning analysis from a repository
description: Deletes a specific code scanning analysis by its ID from a repository; `confirm_delete` must be `true` if it's the last analysis of its type for a given tool and reference to prevent data loss.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository without the `.git` extension (not case sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (not case sensitive).

required.name: analysis_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the code scanning analysis to delete, typically obtained by listing analyses.

optional.name: confirm_delete
optional.description: Pass the string `true` to confirm deletion when this is the last analysis of its type for a specific tool and reference. Required to avoid a 400 error when deleting the final analysis in a set.

title: Delete a codespace for the authenticated user
description: Deletes a specific codespace owned by the authenticated user; this is a destructive action and the codespace must exist.

required.name: codespace_name
required.description: The unique name of the codespace to be deleted. This can be the system-generated name (e.g., 'monalisa-octocat-g4v9wxj96hp') or a user-defined display name if it's unique for the user.

title: Delete a commit comment
description: Deletes a specific commit comment, identified by its `comment_id`, from the specified repository; the comment must exist.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, excluding the `.git` extension. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: comment_id
required.description: The unique numerical identifier of the commit comment to be deleted.

title: Delete a commit comment reaction
description: Deletes a reaction from a commit comment in a GitHub repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: comment_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the commit comment from which the reaction will be deleted.

required.name: reaction_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the reaction to be deleted.

title: Delete commit signature protection
description: Disables GPG commit signature protection for a specific branch in a GitHub repository, meaning commits pushed to this branch no longer require GPG signing.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. The name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This is typically the username of the owner (for personal repositories) or the organization name (for organization-owned repositories). The name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch for which commit signature protection will be disabled. Wildcard characters are not supported in the branch name. To use wildcards, refer to the GitHub GraphQL API.

title: Delete a custom organization role
description: Deletes a custom organization role (which should not be actively assigned) by its ID; a 204 No Content response indicates success.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name (not case-sensitive).

required.name: role_id
required.description: Unique ID of the custom role to delete.

title: Delete dependabot secret by name
description: Deletes a specific Dependabot secret, identified by its name, from a given repository if both the repository and secret exist.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the Dependabot secret to delete. Secret names are case-sensitive and can only contain alphanumeric characters ([A-Z], [a-z], [0-9]) or underscores (_); spaces are not allowed.

title: Delete a deploy key
description: Deletes a specific deploy key from a repository; to change a key's properties or access scope, the existing key must be deleted and a new one created.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: key_id
required.description: The unique identifier (ID) of the deploy key to be deleted.

title: Delete a deployment
description: Permanently deletes a specified *inactive* deployment from a repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the account owning the repository (case-insensitive).

required.name: deployment_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the deployment to delete.

title: Delete a deployment branch policy
description: Deletes a specific deployment branch or tag policy, identified by its ID, from a given environment within a repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: branch_policy_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the branch policy.

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded. For example, any slashes in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.

title: Delete a discussion
description: Deletes a specific team discussion, identified by its number, from an organization's team.

required.name: org
required.description: Case-insensitive name of the organization.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: URL-friendly version (slug) of the team name.

required.name: discussion_number
required.description: The unique number identifying the discussion to be deleted.

title: Delete a discussion comment
description: Deletes a specific comment from an existing team discussion within an organization, provided the specified organization, team, discussion, and comment all exist.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name (not case sensitive).

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name (URL-friendly version).

required.name: comment_number
required.description: Unique number identifying the comment.

required.name: discussion_number
required.description: Unique number identifying the discussion.

title: Delete authenticated user email address
description: Sends an empty request body to `DELETE /user/emails` to attempt deletion of user email addresses; the API typically requires specific emails, so outcome may vary.

required.name: emails
required.description: Array of email addresses to delete from the authenticated user account.

title: Delete an environment
description: Deletes an existing deployment environment from an existing repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This is not case sensitive.

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the environment to delete. The name must be URL encoded; for example, slashes (`/`) should be replaced with `%2F`.

title: Delete an environment secret
description: Deletes an existing and accessible secret from a specified environment within a GitHub repository, returning an empty dictionary on success or error details otherwise.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the secret to be deleted. GitHub stores and processes secret names as uppercase (e.g., `my_secret` becomes `MY_SECRET`).

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the environment from which the secret will be deleted. This name must be URL-encoded if it contains special characters (e.g., slashes `/` should be replaced with `%2F`).

title: Delete an environment variable
description: Deletes a named environment variable from a specified, existing environment within a GitHub repository.

required.name: name
required.description: The name of the environment variable to delete.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the environment. Must be URL-encoded if it contains special characters (e.g., slashes `/` should be `%2F`).

title: Delete a gist
description: Permanently deletes an existing GitHub gist, specified by its `gist_id`; this action is destructive and cannot be undone.

required.name: gist_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the gist to be deleted.

title: Delete a gist comment
description: Deletes a specific comment from a GitHub Gist using its `gist_id` and `comment_id`.

required.name: gist_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the Gist from which the comment will be deleted.

required.name: comment_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the comment to be deleted.

title: Delete GitHub Actions cache by ID
description: Deletes a specific GitHub Actions cache from a repository using its unique `cache_id`.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository.

required.name: cache_id
required.description: The unique ID of the GitHub Actions cache to delete.

title: Delete a GitHub Pages site
description: Deletes the GitHub Pages site for the specified repository; completes without error if no site is currently enabled.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a user or organization). This name is not case-sensitive.

title: Delete an issue comment
description: Permanently deletes a specific comment by its ID from an issue or pull request, if the repository exists and the comment ID is valid.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the account owning the repository (case-insensitive).

required.name: comment_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the comment to delete.

title: Delete an issue comment reaction
description: Deletes a reaction from an issue comment in a repository; the repository, comment, and reaction must exist.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This is not case-sensitive.

required.name: comment_id
required.description: The unique numeric identifier for the issue comment from which the reaction will be deleted.

required.name: reaction_id
required.description: The unique numeric identifier for the reaction to be deleted.

title: Delete an issue reaction
description: Permanently removes a specific reaction from an issue in a GitHub repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: reaction_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the reaction to be deleted.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The unique number identifying the issue from which the reaction will be deleted.

title: Delete a label
description: Permanently removes an existing label from a repository.

required.name: name
required.description: The name of the label to delete. Label names are case-insensitive. If the label name contains spaces or special characters, ensure it is correctly URL-encoded (e.g., 'help wanted' becomes 'help%20wanted').

required.name: repo
required.description: REQUIRED. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Must be provided together with 'owner' to identify the repository (e.g., for 'github.com/octocat/Hello-World', repo is 'Hello-World'). This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: REQUIRED. The username or organization name that owns the repository. GitHub repositories are identified by owner/repo (e.g., 'octocat/Hello-World'), so both 'owner' and 'repo' must be provided together. This field is not case-sensitive.

title: Delete a milestone
description: Deletes the specified milestone if it exists; this operation is idempotent, typically returning a 404 if the milestone is not found or already deleted.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: milestone_number
required.description: The unique number that identifies the milestone to be deleted.

title: Delete an organization
description: Deletes a GitHub organization and its repositories; this is a destructive action and the organization name will be unavailable for reuse for approximately 90 days.

required.name: org
required.description: The unique name of the organization to be deleted. This name is not case-sensitive.

title: Delete an organization secret
description: Permanently deletes a secret from a GitHub organization, making it inaccessible to GitHub Actions workflows or other tools.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the secret to be deleted.

title: Delete an organization variable
description: Deletes a named GitHub Actions variable from a specified organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This parameter is not case-sensitive.

required.name: name
required.description: The name of the organization variable to delete. This parameter is not case-sensitive.

title: Delete an organization webhook
description: Deletes a specific webhook, identified by `hook_id`, from an existing organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: hook_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the webhook. This ID can be retrieved from the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header in a webhook delivery or by listing organization webhooks.

title: Delete a codespace from the organization
description: Permanently deletes a specific codespace belonging to a member of the specified organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization's name (case-insensitive).

required.name: username
required.description: GitHub username of the user owning the codespace.

required.name: codespace_name
required.description: Unique name of the codespace.

title: Delete a package for an organization
description: Deletes a specific package in an organization; cannot delete public packages with over 5,000 downloads.

required.name: org
required.description: Name of the organization owning the package (not case-sensitive).

required.name: package_name
required.description: Unique name of the package to be deleted.

required.name: package_type
required.description: Type of the package to be deleted. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have type `maven`. Docker images in GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have type `container`. Use type `docker` for images previously in GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if migrated to the Container registry.

title: Delete a package for the authenticated user
description: Permanently deletes a specific package owned by the authenticated user; public packages downloaded over 5,000 times cannot be deleted via this API.

required.name: package_name
required.description: The unique name of the package to delete. For npm: supports scoped packages like '@scope/name'. For maven: use format 'com.example.package'. For container/docker: use image name like 'my-app'. The name must match exactly as it appears in the GitHub Packages registry.

required.name: package_type
required.description: The type of package to delete. Supported types: 'npm' (Node.js packages), 'maven' (Java/Gradle packages), 'rubygems' (Ruby gems), 'docker' (legacy Docker images from docker.pkg.github.com), 'nuget' (.NET packages), 'container' (Docker images from ghcr.io). Note: GitHub Gradle packages use 'maven' type; ghcr.io images use 'container' type.

title: Delete package version
description: Tool to delete a package version using GitHub GraphQL API. Use when you need to remove a specific version of a package by its global node ID.

required.name: package_version_id
required.description: The global node ID of the package version to delete (e.g., 'MDEyOlBhY2thZ2VWZXJzaW9uMQ=='). This is the GraphQL ID, not the numeric REST API ID.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. Used to ensure idempotency of mutations.

title: Delete package version for an organization
description: Deletes a specific package version within an organization; requires admin permissions for packages with over 5,000 downloads.

required.name: org
required.description: Organization name (case-insensitive).

required.name: package_name
required.description: Name of the package.

required.name: package_type
required.description:
Package ecosystem. Notes:
- `maven`: For GitHub's Gradle registry packages.
- `container`: For Docker images in GitHub's Container registry (ghcr.io).
- `docker`: For images originally in GitHub's Docker registry (docker.pkg.github.com), including migrated ones.

required.name: package_version_id
required.description: Unique ID of the package version to delete.

title: Delete package version for a user
description: Permanently and irreversibly deletes a specific version of a package owned by the specified user.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the account that owns the package.

required.name: package_name
required.description: The name of the package to which the version belongs.

required.name: package_type
required.description: The type of the package. Supported types include npm, maven, rubygems, docker, nuget, and container. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry use the `maven` type. Docker images in GitHub's Container registry (ghcr.io) use the `container` type. The `docker` type can be used for images previously in GitHub's Docker registry (docker.pkg.github.com), even if migrated.

required.name: package_version_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the package version to be deleted.

title: Delete a pending review for a pull request
description: Deletes a pending (unsubmitted) review from a pull request; this is only possible if the review has not yet been submitted.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: review_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the pending review to be deleted.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: The number that identifies the pull request.

title: Delete a project
description: Deletes the specified GitHub project (Projects V2) using the GraphQL API. Note: This action uses GitHub's Projects V2 GraphQL API. The legacy Projects (classic) REST API was sunset on April 1, 2025 and is no longer available. The project is permanently deleted and cannot be recovered. The user must have admin permissions for the project to delete it.

required.name: project_id
required.description: The unique GraphQL node ID of the project to be deleted (e.g., 'PVT_kwDOBcMqx84ABdPx'). This is returned from project creation or listing operations.

title: Delete a project field (column)
description: Deletes a project field (column) from a GitHub Projects V2 project using the GraphQL API. IMPORTANT: GitHub Classic Projects REST API was sunset on April 1, 2025. This action now uses the GitHub Projects V2 GraphQL API with the deleteProjectV2Field mutation. Note: The built-in Status field cannot be deleted as it is a core field in GitHub Projects V2. Only custom fields can be deleted.

required.name: field_id
required.description: The node ID of the project field to be deleted. This is a GraphQL node ID (e.g., 'PVTF_...').

title: Delete project item for user
description: Tool to delete a project item for a user in GitHub Projects V2. Use when you need to remove an item from a user's project. Requires the project item's GraphQL node ID (starts with 'PVTI_'). Uses the GitHub GraphQL API deleteProjectV2Item mutation.

required.name: item_id
required.description: The GraphQL node ID of the project item to delete (e.g. 'PVTI_lADOBCxhzs4A...').

required.name: username
required.description: The handle for the GitHub user account.

required.name: project_number
required.description: The project's number.

title: Delete a pull request comment reaction
description: Deletes a specific reaction from a pull request review comment, provided the comment and reaction exist on that comment within the specified repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner (username or organization) of the repository; not case-sensitive.

required.name: comment_id
required.description: Unique ID of the pull request review comment.

required.name: reaction_id
required.description: Unique ID of the reaction to delete.

title: Delete pull request review protection
description: Disables the requirement for pull request reviews before merging for a specific, existing branch in an existing repository; this action is idempotent and will succeed even if the protection is not currently enabled.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username or organization name of the repository owner (not case-sensitive).

required.name: branch
required.description: Name of the branch to remove pull request review protection from (wildcards not supported; use GraphQL API for wildcards).

title: Delete repo codespace secret by name
description: Deletes a specific Codespace secret from a repository by its name; this action is idempotent and will succeed even if the secret doesn't exist.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account or the name of the organization that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the Codespace secret to be deleted.

title: Delete social accounts for the authenticated user
description: Deletes currently linked social media account URLs from the authenticated user's GitHub profile.

required.name: account_urls
required.description: Absolute URLs of the social media profiles to be unlinked from the GitHub profile.

title: Delete team discussion comment reaction
description: Deletes a reaction from a team discussion comment, given the organization name, team slug, discussion number, comment number, and reaction ID.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name (URL-friendly version).

required.name: reaction_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the reaction to be deleted.

required.name: comment_number
required.description: The number that uniquely identifies the comment within the discussion.

required.name: discussion_number
required.description: The number that uniquely identifies the discussion.

title: Delete team discussion reaction
description: Permanently deletes a specific reaction from a team discussion within an organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name, which is a URL-friendly version of the team name.

required.name: reaction_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the reaction to be deleted.

required.name: discussion_number
required.description: The unique number identifying the specific discussion within the team.

title: Delete User List
description: Tool to delete a GitHub user list using GraphQL. Use when you need to remove a user list from a GitHub account.

required.name: list_id
required.description: The ID of the user list to delete. This is a GitHub global node ID for the list.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. Used to track requests.

title: Delete a package for a user
description: Deletes a package owned by the specified user, requiring admin permissions for the authenticated user; deletion of public packages with over 5,000 downloads may require GitHub support.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the account that owns the package.

required.name: package_name
required.description: The unique name of the package to be deleted.

required.name: package_type
required.description: Ecosystem of the package. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry use `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) use `container`. The `docker` type can find images from the old Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if migrated.

title: Delete workflow run logs
description: Deletes all logs for a specific workflow run in a GitHub repository, provided the repository and run exist.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run.

title: Disable a custom protection rule for an environment
description: Disables a specific, currently active custom deployment protection rule for an existing environment within a GitHub repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository (without the `.git` extension). This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a user or organization). This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the environment. This name must be URL encoded; for example, any slashes (`/`) in the name must be replaced with `%2F`.

required.name: protection_rule_id
required.description: The unique integer identifier of the custom deployment protection rule to be disabled.

title: Disable a workflow
description: Disables a specified workflow (by ID or filename) in a given GitHub repository, preventing new automatic triggers; any in-progress runs will continue.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: workflow_id
required.description: The ID of the workflow or the workflow's file name (e.g., `main.yml` or `ci.yaml`). You can obtain the workflow ID by listing workflows in a repository.

title: Disable private vulnerability reporting for a repository
description: Disables private vulnerability reporting for an existing GitHub repository, preventing direct private vulnerability reports to maintainers via GitHub's interface for this repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

title: Disable Repository Actions In Org
description: Removes a repository from the list of selected repositories enabled for GitHub Actions in an organization. Only works when the organization's `enabled_repositories` policy is set to `selected`. Requires admin:org scope.

required.name: org
required.description: The GitHub organization name (not case-sensitive).

required.name: repository_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the repository.

title: Dismiss a review for a pull request
description: Dismisses an APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED review on a pull request with a mandatory explanatory message. IMPORTANT: Only reviews in APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED state can be dismissed. Reviews in COMMENTED, PENDING, or already DISMISSED state will return a 422 error. To dismiss a review on a protected branch, you must be a repository admin or be authorized to dismiss pull request reviews.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: message
required.description: The reason for dismissing the review. This is a required field.

required.name: review_id
required.description: The unique identifier for the review to be dismissed. The review must be in APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED state.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: The unique number identifying the pull request within the repository.

optional.name: event
optional.description: The event type for dismissing the review. Must be set to DISMISS.

title: Download an artifact
description: Downloads a GitHub Actions workflow artifact as a ZIP file. Returns the artifact as a downloadable file. Use GITHUB_LIST_ARTIFACTS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY or GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUN_ARTIFACTS to get valid artifact IDs first.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username or organization name of the repository owner (case-insensitive).

required.name: artifact_id
required.description: Unique numeric identifier of the artifact. Obtain from GITHUB_LIST_ARTIFACTS_FOR_A_REPOSITORY or GITHUB_LIST_WORKFLOW_RUN_ARTIFACTS actions.

optional.name: archive_format
optional.description: Archive format for the download. GitHub API only supports 'zip'. Defaults to 'zip'.

title: Download a repository tarball
description: Downloads a repository's source code as a tarball (.tar.gz) archive for a specific Git reference, if the repository is accessible.

required.name: ref
required.description: A Git reference (e.g., branch name, tag name, or commit SHA) that points to the specific version of the repository content to be downloaded as a tarball archive. For example, `main` for the main branch, `v1.0.0` for a tag, or a full commit SHA.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

title: Download a repository archive ZIP
description: Downloads a repository's source code as a ZIP archive for a specific Git reference (branch, tag, or commit SHA). IMPORTANT SIZE LIMITATION: This action may fail with 'payload too large' errors for large repositories due to platform size restrictions. If you encounter size limit issues, consider these alternatives: - Use GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT to fetch specific files or directories (also lists directory contents) - Clone the repository using git if you need the full codebase Best suited for: small to medium repositories, downloading specific tagged releases, or quick code inspection.

required.name: ref
required.description: The Git reference for the archive. This can be a branch name, a tag name, or a commit SHA.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This is not case-sensitive.

title: Download job logs for a workflow run
description: Downloads logs for a specific job in a GitHub Actions workflow run, contingent on the repository's existence and the job ID being valid and having produced logs.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., user or organization). This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: job_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the job for which to download logs. You can obtain this from the 'List jobs for a workflow run' endpoint.

title: Download workflow run attempt logs
description: Downloads a ZIP archive of logs for a specific workflow run attempt. Returns a downloadable ZIP file containing logs for all jobs and steps in the workflow run.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run.

required.name: attempt_number
required.description: The attempt number of the workflow run.

title: Download workflow run logs
description: Downloads logs for a specific GitHub Actions workflow run as a ZIP archive containing log files for each job in the workflow.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository (e.g., 'Spoon-Knife') without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., 'octocat'). This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run (e.g., 12345).

title: Enable a workflow
description: Reactivates a currently disabled GitHub Actions workflow within a repository using its workflow ID or filename.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: workflow_id
required.description: The ID of the workflow to be enabled. You can provide either the numeric workflow ID (e.g., 30433642) or the workflow filename (e.g., 'ci.yaml', 'data.yml').

title: Enable GitHub actions in selected repositories
description: Sets the specific repositories that can use GitHub Actions within an organization by replacing the current list; only applies if the organization's Actions policy is 'selected repositories'.

required.name: org
required.description: Name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive).

required.name: selected_repository_ids
required.description: List of unique repository IDs for which GitHub Actions will be enabled. This list completely replaces the current selection of repositories.

title: Enable private vulnerability reporting for a repository
description: Enables private vulnerability reporting for a repository, allowing security researchers to privately submit vulnerability reports to maintainers.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This is typically the username or organization name and is not case-sensitive.

title: Enable repo for Github Actions
description: Adds a repository to the list of selected repositories enabled for GitHub Actions in an organization. Requires the organization's 'enabled_repositories' policy to be set to 'selected'.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: repository_id
required.description: The unique numerical identifier of the GitHub repository.

title: Encrypt and update dev secret
description: Creates or updates a repository's development environment secret using an `encrypted_value` and its corresponding `key_id`; the secret must be pre-encrypted with the repository's Codespaces public key.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the development environment secret.

optional.name: key_id
optional.description: ID of the public key (retrieved from the GitHub API's 'Get a repository public key for Codespaces' endpoint: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/codespaces/secrets/public-key`) used to encrypt the secret's value. If not provided, it will be fetched automatically.

optional.name: secret_value
optional.description: The plaintext value for your secret. This will be automatically encrypted using the repository's Codespaces public key before being sent to GitHub. If you already have an encrypted value, use the encrypted_value parameter instead.

optional.name: encrypted_value

title: Encrypt org dev env secret

required.name: secret_name

optional.name: secret_value
optional.description: The plaintext value for your secret. This will be automatically encrypted using the organization's Codespaces public key before being sent to GitHub. If you already have an encrypted value, use the encrypted_value parameter instead.

optional.name: encrypted_value

required.name: codespace_name
required.description: Unique name of the codespace to be exported.

title: Export an SBOM for a repository
description: Exports the software bill of materials (SBOM) in SPDX JSON format for a repository, if its dependency graph is enabled and it has at least one commit.

title: Find Pull Requests
description: Primary tool to find and search pull requests. Supports filtering by repository, author, state, labels, and merge status, and returns structured PR data for reliable use in workflows. GitHub search results are capped at ~1000 total items; narrow filters when totals approach this limit. `created_since`/`updated_since` filter on creation/update timestamps, not `merged_at`; apply merge-date filtering client-side.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results to fetch.

optional.name: repo
optional.description: Filter by specific repository. Can be provided in 'owner/repo' format (e.g., 'facebook/react'), or as just the repo name when used with the owner parameter. When owner and repo are both provided and have the same value, they are combined as 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with owner, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The repository must exist and be accessible with your token. Prefer 'owner/repo' format; bare repo name without the `owner` parameter causes invalid repository format errors.

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Field to sort results by. Set explicitly to 'updated' with `order=desc` when recency matters; default behavior may return best-match relevance ordering instead.

optional.name: label
optional.description: Filter by label name.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Sort order (ascending or descending).

optional.name: owner
optional.description: Filter by repository owner (user or organization). Can be used alone to search all repositories for an owner, or combined with repo parameter to specify owner and repo separately. When both owner and repo are provided, the search is scoped to 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with repo, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The owner must exist and repositories must be accessible with your token.

optional.name: query
optional.description: Optional search query for PR title, description, or commit messages. Supports GitHub search syntax including label filters (e.g., 'label:bug'), logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), and text search. If not provided, PRs will be listed based on other filter parameters. Type qualifiers (type:pr, is:pr, is:issue, type:issue) are automatically normalized. When using logical operators with qualifiers like labels, the query is automatically grouped for proper parsing. When omitting query, ensure at least one structured filter parameter is provided; passing no query and no filters may cause validation errors. Prefer dedicated parameters (`label`, `state`, `author`) over embedding qualifiers in the query string. Exact title matching is not supported; post-filter on title client-side if needed.

optional.name: state
optional.description: Filter by PR state: 'open', 'closed', or 'all'.

optional.name: author
optional.description: Filter by PR author username. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

optional.name: assignee
optional.description: Filter by PR assignee username. Use '@me' for current user. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

optional.name: language
optional.description: Filter by programming language.

optional.name: mentions
optional.description: Filter by username mentioned in PR. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100). GitHub caps total search results at ~1000 items; iterate `page` until results fewer than `per_page` are returned, and add `repo`, `label`, or date filters when totals approach 1000.

optional.name: is_merged
optional.description: Filter by merge status. True for merged PRs, False for unmerged, None for all.

optional.name: base_branch
optional.description: Filter by base branch name.

optional.name: head_branch
optional.description: Filter by head branch name.

optional.name: created_since
optional.description: Filter PRs created after this date (ISO 8601 format). Provide as UTC ISO 8601 timestamp to avoid off-by-one-day errors at range boundaries. Does not filter on `merged_at`.

optional.name: updated_since
optional.description: Filter PRs updated after this date (ISO 8601 format).

optional.name: response_detail
optional.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.

optional.name: for_authenticated_user
optional.description: Include private repositories accessible to the authenticated user in search results. When True without repo/owner, searches PRs involving you (author, assignee, mentions, commenter) across all accessible repos. When False without repo/owner, restricts to public repos only. When repo/owner is specified, this flag has no effect on scope. Set to True when searching private repositories; False searches all of GitHub and produces large noisy result sets.

title: Find Repositories
description: AI-optimized repository search with smart filtering by language, stars, topics, and ownership. Builds intelligent search queries and returns clean, actionable repository data. Check `incomplete_results` in the response — when true, results are non-exhaustive. Search endpoints are rate-limited to ~30 requests/minute (vs. 5000/hour for general REST); apply backoff on 403/429. Total results are capped at ~1000 per query regardless of pagination.

required.name: query
required.description: Search query for repository name, description, or README content. Accepts both 'query' and 'q' as parameter names. Supports OR operator for alternatives (e.g., 'bug OR error'). Multi-word phrases in OR expressions are automatically quoted. GitHub limits OR expressions to 6 terms maximum; queries exceeding this limit are truncated. If using GitHub qualifiers like 'repo:', 'user:', or 'org:', they must be properly formatted (e.g., 'repo:owner/name', 'user:username', 'org:orgname'). Note: 'owner:' is not a valid GitHub qualifier; if used, it will be automatically transformed to 'user:'. Must be non-empty; blank strings trigger a 'Search query cannot be empty' validation error.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results to fetch.

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Field to sort results by.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Sort order (ascending or descending).

optional.name: owner
optional.description: Filter by specific user or organization. Do NOT use this parameter if your 'query' already contains 'user:', 'org:', or 'repo:' qualifiers - they will conflict. Use either 'owner' parameter OR search qualifiers in 'query', not both.

optional.name: topic
optional.description: Filter by repository topic/tag.

optional.name: archived
optional.description: Filter by archived status. None means include both.

optional.name: language
optional.description: Filter by programming language.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100). GitHub caps total results at ~1000 per query; for exhaustive searches, split by `language`, `topic`, `min_stars`/`max_stars`, or `owner`.

optional.name: max_stars
optional.description: Maximum number of stars the repository should have.

optional.name: min_forks
optional.description: Minimum number of forks the repository should have.

optional.name: min_stars
optional.description: Minimum number of stars the repository should have.

optional.name: fork_filter
optional.description: How to handle forks: 'include' (include forks), 'exclude' (exclude forks), 'only' (only forks).

optional.name: response_detail
optional.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.

optional.name: for_authenticated_user
optional.description: Search only in repositories accessible to the authenticated user (including private repos). Requires token scopes `repo`/`read:org`; sparse results compared to GitHub UI typically indicate insufficient token scopes.

description: Generates Markdown release notes content (listing changes, pull requests, and contributors) for a GitHub repository release, customizable via tags and a configuration file.

description: Lists users, teams, and GitHub Apps with push access to a branch; this branch must be protected in repository settings for detailed restrictions, otherwise expect a 404 or empty response.

For more information, see "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" in the Git documentation.

title: Get a reference
description: Retrieves a specific Git reference (e.g., a branch, tag, or fully qualified like 'heads/main') from a GitHub repository. The reference must exist in the repository; use 'list_matching_references' first if unsure what references are available.

required.name: ref
required.description: The Git reference to retrieve. Must be formatted as `heads/<branch_name>` for branches, `tags/<tag_name>` for tags, or `pull/<number>/head` (or `pull/<number>/merge`) for pull requests. Simple branch names (e.g., `main`) are automatically converted to `heads/<name>`. The reference must exist in the repository; a 404 error is returned if not found. If unsure which references exist, use 'list_matching_references' or 'get_a_branch' first. Note: Commit SHAs are not supported by this endpoint; use commit-specific endpoints instead. Not all repositories use 'master'; many now use 'main' as the default branch.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

title: List repository files and directories

Ensure owner, repo, ref, and path are consistent when combining with other GitHub tools to avoid mismatched-ref errors.

required.name: path

Do NOT pass a full GitHub URL - only the relative path within the repo. Must exactly match the file path as it exists in the repository — use GITHUB_GET_A_TREE to discover valid paths rather than guessing directory structure.

required.description: The repository name (not the full URL). This is the repository name shown in the repository URL (e.g., for github.com/torvalds/linux, the repo is 'linux'). Do not include '.git' suffix. Case-insensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The GitHub username or organization name that owns the repository. This is the account name shown in the repository URL (e.g., for github.com/torvalds/linux, the owner is 'torvalds'). Case-insensitive.

optional.name: ref
optional.description: The branch name, tag name, or commit SHA to fetch the file from. Defaults to the repository's default branch (usually 'main' or 'master'). Recommended to pass explicitly — omitting it fetches from the default branch, which may not match the ref used in other tool calls and can yield unexpected or missing content.

title: Get repository content

required.name: path
required.description: Required. Path to file or directory in the repository. Empty string ('') retrieves root directory contents. Leading slashes auto-stripped. CRITICAL: Do NOT pass branch names here (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main'). Branch names belong in the `ref` parameter. Path should be file/directory path only (e.g., 'src/main.js', 'README.md'), NOT prefixed with branch name (use 'src/main.js' not 'main/src/main.js'). File paths must include extension (e.g., 'README.md', not 'README'). For common files (README, LICENSE, CHANGELOG) without extensions, action auto-tries common extensions (.md, .txt, .rst). Paths are case-sensitive. On 404 errors, list parent directory to verify exact path/casing.

required.name: repo
required.description: Required. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Required. The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive. Can also accept full repository path in format 'owner/repo' - the repo part will be extracted automatically.

optional.name: ref
optional.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag to read from. Use this parameter to specify which branch (e.g., 'feat/godlocal-dev', 'main', 'develop'), tag (e.g., 'v1.2.0'), or commit SHA you want to access. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used. Note: Branch names should be passed here, NOT in the path parameter.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

title: Get repository secret securely
description: Retrieves metadata for an existing Dependabot secret in a repository, without exposing its encrypted value.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the Dependabot secret to retrieve.

title: Get repository security advisory
description: Tool to retrieve a repository security advisory using its GHSA identifier. Use when you need detailed information about a specific security vulnerability.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: ghsa_id
required.description: The GHSA (GitHub Security Advisory) identifier of the advisory.

title: Get a delivery for a repository webhook
description: Retrieves a specific delivery for a repository webhook, identified by its `hook_id` and `delivery_id`.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: hook_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the webhook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery, or by listing repository webhooks.

required.name: delivery_id
required.description: The unique identifier of a specific delivery for the webhook. This ID corresponds to a single delivery attempt. You can find this by listing webhook deliveries.

title: Get rules for a branch
description: Retrieves all active rules for a specific branch in a GitHub repository, excluding rules in 'evaluate' or 'disabled' status.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The GitHub account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch. Wildcard characters are not supported for this parameter; to use wildcards, refer to the GitHub GraphQL API.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results to fetch.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (max 100).

title: Get Organization Dependabot Secret
description: Gets a single organization Dependabot secret's metadata (name, timestamps, visibility) without revealing its encrypted value. Requires admin:org scope.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive).

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the Dependabot secret to retrieve (case-insensitive).

title: Get status checks protection
description: Retrieves the status check protection settings for a specific branch in a GitHub repository, if status check protection is enabled for it.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch. Wildcard characters are not supported in branch names for this endpoint; for wildcard support, please refer to the GitHub GraphQL API.

title: Get team members
description: Retrieves a list of members for a specific team within an organization. Returns team members including members of child teams. Use this action when you need to see who belongs to a team, optionally filtered by their role (member or maintainer). Requires the authenticated user to have read access to the team within the organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name. This is the URL-friendly version of the team name.

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number of the results to fetch. Used for pagination.

optional.name: role
optional.description: Filters members returned by their role in the team. Can be 'member' for regular team members, 'maintainer' for team maintainers, or 'all' to include both.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results per page. Maximum is 100.

title: Get team membership for a user
description: Retrieves a user's role and membership status within a specific team in an organization. Returns membership details including role ('member' or 'maintainer') and state ('active' or 'pending'). If the user is not a member of the team, returns is_member=False with a descriptive message. Requires the authenticated user to be an organization member with visibility into the team.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the user.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The URL-friendly version of the team name (slug).

title: Get teams with access to the protected branch
description: Lists teams with explicit push access to a protected branch, provided team restrictions are configured in the branch's protection settings; returns an empty list otherwise.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension; not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the repository owner; not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: Name of the branch; does not support wildcard characters (for wildcard support, use the GraphQL API).

title: Get the authenticated user
description: Gets the profile information for the currently authenticated GitHub user, including potentially private details based on user settings.

title: Get the combined status for a specific reference
description: Retrieves the aggregated commit status (e.g., success, failure, pending) from all checks for a specific reference (SHA, branch, or tag) in a GitHub repository.

required.name: ref
required.description: The specific commit reference to query. This can be a commit SHA, a branch name (e.g., `heads/main`), or a tag name (e.g., `tags/v1.0.0`). See "[Git References](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Git-References)" for more details.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number for the results to retrieve. See "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)" for more information.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results to display per page, with a maximum of 100. Details on pagination can be found in "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

title: Get the hourly commit count for each day
description: Retrieves the 'punch card' data, showing hourly commit counts for each day of the week for an existing and accessible repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This is typically the username or organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

title: Get the last year of commit activity
description: Fetches weekly commit totals and daily commit counts for the last 52 weeks for a specified GitHub repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

title: Get the latest release
description: Fetches the latest official (non-prerelease, non-draft) release for a GitHub repository; requires at least one such published release.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

title: Get the license for a repository
description: Retrieves the license file and its details for a repository, optionally from a specific Git reference (branch, tag, or commit SHA).

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: ref
optional.description: The specific Git reference (branch name, tag name, or commit SHA) to retrieve the license from. For a branch, it can be formatted as `refs/heads/<branch_name>` or simply `<branch_name>`. To reference a pull request's merge commit, use `refs/pull/<pull_number>/merge`. If omitted, the license from the repository's default branch is used.

title: Get the review history for a workflow run
description: Retrieves the detailed approval history for a specific workflow run in a GitHub repository, detailing each review's environment, state, reviewer, and comments, to track the approval process for workflows, particularly automated deployments.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account or the name of the organization that owns the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run for which to retrieve the review history.

title: Get the status of a GitHub Pages deployment
description: Retrieves the status of a specific GitHub Pages deployment for a repository, which must have GitHub Pages enabled.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: pages_deployment_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the GitHub Pages deployment. This can be the numeric ID of the deployment or the commit SHA that triggered the deployment.

title: Get the weekly commit activity
description: Fetches the weekly commit activity (additions and deletions per week) for a repository over the past year; best for repositories with under 10,000 commits.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a user or organization). This name is not case-sensitive.

title: Get the weekly commit count
description: Retrieves the weekly commit count for a repository, detailing commits by the owner and all contributors over the last 52 weeks; GitHub may return a 202 status or an empty response if statistics are being computed.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

title: Get the Zen of GitHub
description: Retrieves a random quote from GitHub's 'Zen of GitHub' collection, reflecting GitHub's design philosophies and offering humorous insights, useful for displaying GitHub wisdom or a lighthearted message.

title: Get top referral paths
description: Fetches the top 10 most viewed content paths for a repository from the last 14 days.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the account or organization owning the repository (not case-sensitive).

title: Get top referral sources
description: Fetches the top 10 websites that referred traffic to a repository within the last 14 days.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is case-insensitive.

title: Get user by ID
description: Retrieves a GitHub user's profile information by their unique numeric account ID. Use when you know the user's numeric ID rather than their username.

required.name: account_id
required.description: The unique numeric identifier of the GitHub user account to retrieve.

title: Get user project item
description: Tool to get an item from a user-owned project in GitHub Projects V2. Use when you need to retrieve details about a specific item (issue, pull request, or draft issue) in a user's project board.

required.name: item_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the project item.

required.name: username
required.description: The handle for the GitHub user account.

required.name: project_number
required.description: The project's number.

optional.name: fields
optional.description: Limit results to specific fields, by their IDs. If not specified, the title field will be returned. Example: fields[]=123&fields[]=456&fields[]=789 or fields=123,456,789

title: Get user attestations by subject digest
description: Tool to get attestations by subject digest for a GitHub user. Use when you need to retrieve attestation data for a specific artifact or resource identified by its subject digest.

required.name: username
required.description: The handle for the GitHub user account.

required.name: subject_digest
required.description: Subject digest for the attestation. Must include the algorithm prefix (e.g., 'sha256:' or 'sha512:').

optional.name: after
optional.description: A cursor, as given in the Link header. If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor.

optional.name: before
optional.description: A cursor, as given in the Link header. If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

optional.name: predicate_type
optional.description: Optional filter for fetching attestations with a given predicate type. This option accepts 'provenance', 'sbom', 'release', or freeform text for custom predicate types.

title: Get user's projects v2
description: Tool to list GitHub Projects v2 for a specified user. Use when you need to retrieve all projects owned by a user with pagination support.

required.name: username
required.description: The handle for the GitHub user account.

optional.name: q
optional.description: Limit results to projects of the specified type.

optional.name: after
optional.description: A cursor, as given in the Link header. If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

optional.name: before
optional.description: A cursor, as given in the Link header. If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

title: Get Viewer via GraphQL

title: Get workflow external access level

required.name: owner

title: Get a job for a workflow run
description: Retrieves detailed information for a specific job within a GitHub Actions workflow run, given its `job_id` which must be valid for the specified repository's workflow.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner

title: Get workflow run usage
description: Gets the billable time, in milliseconds, for a specific workflow run, detailing time spent on various operating systems.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: run_id

title: Get workflow usage
description: Gets the billable time (in milliseconds, broken down by runner OS) for a specific workflow within a repository for the current billing cycle.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: workflow_id
required.description: The unique identifier (ID) of the workflow or the workflow's file name (e.g., 'main.yml').

title: Check if repo starred by auth user
description: Use to determine if the authenticated user has starred a specific GitHub repository, which is confirmed by an HTTP 204 status (resulting in an empty dictionary in the response data); the action fails (e.g., HTTP 404) if the repository is not starred or does not exist.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a user or organization). This name is not case sensitive.

title: List accepted assignments for an assignment
description: Lists accepted assignments (student repositories created after acceptance) for an existing GitHub Classroom assignment, identified by its unique `assignment_id`.

required.description: The unique identifier of the classroom assignment for which to list accepted assignments.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to retrieve.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results to return per page (maximum 100).

title: List repositories accessible via GitHub App installation
description: Lists repositories that the authenticated user can access through a specific GitHub App installation. Returns repositories where the user has explicit :read, :write, or :admin permission through the installation. The response includes permission details for each repository. Prerequisites: - Requires a GitHub App user access token (not a standard OAuth token) - Use GITHUB_LIST_APP_INSTALLATIONS first to get valid installation IDs

required.name: installation_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the GitHub App installation. Get this from GITHUB_LIST_APP_INSTALLATIONS.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to fetch, starting from 1.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of repositories to return per page. Maximum is 100.

title: List app installations for user token
description: Lists GitHub App installations accessible to the authenticated user via their access token, including installation details, permissions, and repository access.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results to retrieve.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (max 100).

title: Get apps with access to the protected branch
description: Lists GitHub Apps with push access to a repository's protected branch.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the '.git' extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the protected branch. This name cannot contain wildcard characters. To work with branch names containing wildcard characters, please use the GitHub GraphQL API.

title: List artifacts for a repository
description: Lists GitHub Actions workflow artifacts for a specified repository, which must exist.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: name
optional.description: The name of an artifact. If specified, only artifacts with this exact name will be returned. If omitted or null, all artifacts in the repository are listed (subject to pagination).

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number of the results to fetch, starting from 1.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of artifacts to return per page; maximum is 100.

title: List assignees
description: Lists users who can be assigned to issues in a repository, typically those with push access.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results (1-indexed).

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page. Max 100.

title: List assignments for a classroom

optional.name: page
optional.description: Specifies the page number of the results to retrieve. For more information, refer to GitHub's documentation on [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Specifies the number of results to return per page (maximum is 100). For more information, refer to GitHub's documentation on [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

title: List attestation repositories
