optional.name: after
optional.description: A cursor, as given in the Link header. If specified, the query only searches for results after this cursor. For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

optional.name: before
optional.description: A cursor, as given in the Link header. If specified, the query only searches for results before this cursor. For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

title: List available machine types for a repository
description: Lists machine types available for GitHub Codespaces in a repository, optionally using a Git ref to check compatibility based on prebuild availability and devcontainer configurations.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This is typically the username (for personal repositories) or the organization name (for organization-owned repositories). The name is not case sensitive.

optional.name: ref
optional.description: The Git reference (branch name, tag name, or commit SHA) to check for prebuild availability and devcontainer configuration restrictions. This ensures listed machine types are compatible with the specified repository version.

optional.name: location
optional.description: The geographic location to check for available machine types. If not provided, the location may be inferred. Specifying a location can help find machines in a preferred region.

optional.name: client_ip
optional.description: An IP address used for auto-detecting the location if `location` is not specified. This is particularly useful when requests are proxied, to ensure location-based machine availability is accurate.

title: List branches
description: List branches in a GitHub repository. Returns branch names, commit information, and protection status. Use this action when you need to retrieve all branches in a repository, optionally filtered by protection status. This is useful for identifying available branches, checking which branches are protected, or preparing to create pull requests.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number of the results to fetch. For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results per page (max 100). For more information, see 'Using pagination in the REST API'.

optional.name: protected
optional.description: Setting to `true` returns only branches protected by branch protections or rulesets. When set to `false`, only unprotected branches are returned. Omitting this parameter returns all branches.

title: List branches for head commit
description: Lists branches in an accessible repository where the provided commit SHA is the head, useful for identifying development lines based on that commit.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a user or organization). This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: commit_sha
required.description: The full SHA-1 hash of the commit. This action will find branches where this commit is the most recent one (the head).

title: List check run annotations

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner

required.name: check_run_id

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number of the results to fetch. See "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)" for more details.

optional.name: per_page

title: List check runs for a git ref
description: List GitHub check runs for a commit SHA, branch, or tag to assess CI status and conclusions. Use when you need reliable CI pass/fail signals beyond commit metadata.

required.name: owner

optional.description: Page number of the results to retrieve.

title: List commits
description: Lists commits for a GitHub repository. Requires 'owner' (username/org) and 'repo' (repository name) parameters. Optionally filter by SHA/branch, path, author, committer, or date range.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension (repository name only, not the full 'owner/repo' path). Must contain only alphanumeric characters, hyphens (-), underscores (_), and periods (.). Wildcards like '*' are not supported.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name only, not the full 'owner/repo' path). Must contain only alphanumeric characters and hyphens, cannot start/end with a hyphen, max 39 characters. Wildcards are not supported.

optional.name: sha
optional.description: SHA hash or branch name to start listing commits from. If not provided, the GitHub API uses the repository's default branch (usually `main` or `master`).

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to fetch when using pagination.

optional.name: path
optional.description: Only commits modifying this specific file path will be returned.

optional.name: since
optional.description: Only commits created on or after this timestamp will be returned. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

optional.name: until
optional.description: Only commits created before this timestamp will be returned. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

optional.name: author
optional.description: Filter commits by the commit author's GitHub login or email address.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results to return per page (max 100).

optional.name: committer
optional.description: Filter commits by the commit committer's GitHub login or email address. The committer is the user who applied the patch and may differ from the original author.

title: List commits on a pull request

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number of the results to fetch.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results per page (maximum 100).

optional.description: Specifies the page number of the results to fetch. Default is 1. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Specifies the number of results to return per page, with a maximum of 100. Default is 30. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

title: List users blocked by the authenticated user
description: Lists users blocked by the authenticated user, returning an empty list if no users are blocked.

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number of the results to retrieve.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of results per page (max 100).

title: List users assigned org role
description: Lists users assigned to a specific role within a GitHub organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This is not case-sensitive.

required.name: role_id
required.description: The unique identifier for the organization role. Use the 'Get all organization roles' action first to retrieve valid role IDs.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results (1-indexed).

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100).

title: List watchers
description: Retrieves a list of users watching a specific repository; the repository must be accessible to the authenticated user.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to retrieve.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results to return per page (max 100).

title: List workflow run artifacts
description: Lists artifacts (e.g., build outputs, test results) for a specific workflow run in a GitHub repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (not case sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (not case sensitive).

required.name: run_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the workflow run.

optional.name: name
optional.description: If specified, filters artifacts by this exact name.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results to fetch.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (max 100).

title: List workflow runs for a repository
description: Lists workflow runs for a repository, allowing filtering by actor, branch, event, status, creation date, check suite ID, or head SHA; the repository must exist and be accessible.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to fetch.

optional.name: actor
optional.description: Filter by the actor's login (e.g., the user who triggered the `push`).

optional.name: event
optional.description: Filter by the event that triggered the workflow (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`).

optional.name: branch
optional.description: Filter by branch name (e.g., `main` or the branch that triggered the `push`).

optional.name: status
optional.description: Filter by `status` or `conclusion` (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

optional.name: created
optional.description: Filter by creation date or date-time range (ISO8601 format: YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ). Supports operators like `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=`, and `..` for ranges.

optional.name: head_sha
optional.description: Filter to include only runs associated with the specified `head_sha` (commit SHA at the head of the branch).

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100).

optional.name: check_suite_id
optional.description: Filter by a specific `check_suite_id`.

optional.name: exclude_pull_requests
optional.description: Set to `true` to exclude workflow runs triggered by pull request events. Omit or leave as null to include all runs.

title: List workflow runs for a workflow
description: Lists runs for a specified, existing workflow (identified by ID or filename like `main.yml`) in a GitHub repository, with filtering options.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

required.name: workflow_id
required.description: The ID of the workflow (integer) or the workflow file name (string, e.g., `main.yml` or `ci.yaml`).

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to retrieve.

optional.name: actor
optional.description: Filter by the GitHub username of the actor who initiated the run.

optional.name: event
optional.description: Filter by the event that triggered the run (e.g., `push`, `pull_request`). For more event types, see GitHub's documentation on "Events that trigger workflows".

optional.name: branch
optional.description: Filter by branch name, typically for `push` events.

optional.name: status
optional.description: Filter by status or conclusion (e.g., `success`, `in_progress`). Note: `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested` statuses are set exclusively by GitHub Actions.

optional.name: created
optional.description: Filter by creation date/time range. For syntax, refer to GitHub's "Understanding the search syntax" guide for dates.

optional.name: head_sha
optional.description: Filter by the head commit's SHA.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (max 100).

optional.name: check_suite_id
optional.description: Filter by `check_suite_id` (identifier for a collection of check runs).

optional.name: exclude_pull_requests
optional.description: If true, exclude workflow runs triggered by pull requests.

title: Lock an issue
description: Locks an existing GitHub issue's conversation, preventing further comments; an optional reason can be specified.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The number that uniquely identifies the issue to be locked within the repository.

optional.name: lock_reason
optional.description: Optional reason for locking the conversation. Valid values: 'off-topic', 'too heated', 'resolved', 'spam'. If omitted, no reason is displayed.

title: Lookup Enterprise Administrator Invitation
description: Tool to look up a pending enterprise administrator invitation by invitee, enterprise, and role. Use when you need to check if a specific user has a pending invitation to become an enterprise administrator.

required.name: role
required.description: The role for the enterprise administrator invitation. Must be one of: OWNER, BILLING_MANAGER, or UNAFFILIATED.

required.name: user_login
required.description: The login (username) of the user invited to join the enterprise as an administrator.

required.name: enterprise_slug
required.description: The slug of the enterprise the user was invited to join. This is the URL-friendly identifier for the enterprise.

title: Lookup GitHub Resource
description: Tool to lookup a GitHub resource by its URL. Use when you need to identify or retrieve information about a GitHub resource from its URL.

required.name: url
required.description: The GitHub URL of the resource to lookup. Can be a repository, issue, pull request, or other GitHub resource URL.

title: Lookup nodes by IDs
description: Tool to lookup GitHub nodes by their global node IDs. Use when you need to retrieve multiple objects by their IDs in a single batch query.

required.name: ids
required.description: A list of GitHub global node IDs to lookup. Each ID must be a valid base64-encoded global node ID (e.g., 'MDQ6VXNlcjU4MzIzMQ==').

title: Lookup Organization (GraphQL)
description: Tool to lookup a GitHub organization by login using GraphQL. Use when you need organization information via GraphQL API.

required.name: login
required.description: The organization's login username to look up. Case-sensitive.

title: Look Up Topic by Name
description: Tool to look up a GitHub topic by name using GraphQL. Use when you need to find information about a specific GitHub topic including its popularity (stargazer count) and related topics.

required.name: name
required.description: The topic's name to look up (e.g., 'python', 'javascript', 'machine-learning').

optional.name: related_topics_count
optional.description: The number of related topics to fetch (between 1 and 10). Only used if include_related_topics is true.

optional.name: include_related_topics
optional.description: Whether to include related topics in the response. If true, up to 3 related topics will be returned.

title: Manage access control for organization codespaces
description: Sets the Codespaces access control policy for a GitHub organization, determining which members can use them. This endpoint requires admin permissions on the organization. The API returns HTTP 204 No Content on success.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive). The authenticated user must have admin permissions on this organization.

required.name: visibility
required.description:
Defines which users can access Codespaces within the organization.
`disabled`: Codespaces are disabled for all users in the organization.
`selected_members`: Only users specified in `selected_usernames` can access Codespaces.
`all_members`: All members of the organization can access Codespaces.
`all_members_and_outside_collaborators`: All members and outside collaborators can access Codespaces.

optional.name: selected_usernames
optional.description: A list of GitHub usernames who should have access to Codespaces. Required when `visibility` is set to `selected_members`. Providing a list here will replace any existing list of selected usernames. The specified users must be members or outside collaborators of the organization.

title: Manage custom properties for org repos
description: Creates or updates values for an organization's predefined custom properties across multiple repositories (up to 30).

required.name: org
required.description: The organization's name (case-insensitive).

required.name: properties
required.description: JSON string containing an array of custom properties to set. Each must have `property_name` (predefined for the organization) and `value`. Example: '[{"property_name": "project-status", "value": "active"}]'

required.name: repository_names
required.description: Repository names (max 30) to apply the custom property values to.

title: Manage issue blocking dependency
description: Add or remove an issue that blocks another issue in the same repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name.

required.name: owner
required.description: Repository owner.

required.name: operation
required.description: Whether to add or remove the blocked-by relationship.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: Number of the issue being blocked.

required.name: blocking_issue_id
required.description: Global database ID of the blocking issue, not its repository issue number.

title: List selected repositories for a GitHub Actions organization secret
description: Lists repositories within an organization that have been explicitly granted access to a specific GitHub Actions organization secret. Returns all repositories that have been selected when the visibility for repository access to an Actions secret is set to 'selected'. Requires admin:org scope and admin access to the organization. Note: This endpoint only returns results when the secret's visibility is set to 'selected'. Secrets with visibility 'all' or 'private' do not have specific repository selections.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the organization secret for which to list accessible repositories.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to fetch. Default is 1. See '[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)' for more details.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results to return per page (maximum 100). Default is 30. See '[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)' for more details.

title: Mark a thread as done
description: Marks the GitHub notification thread (identified by `thread_id`) as done or read for the authenticated user, effectively archiving it.

required.name: thread_id
required.description: ID of the notification thread to mark as done. Typically obtained from the `id` field in notification list operations (e.g., `GET /notifications`).

title: Mark a thread as read
description: Marks an existing GitHub notification thread, identified by its `thread_id`, as read.

required.name: thread_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the notification thread. This ID is obtained from a notification's `id` field, for example, via the 'List notifications for the authenticated user' endpoint.

title: Mark notifications as read
description: Marks notifications as read or unread, optionally for those updated at or before a `last_read_at` timestamp.

optional.name: read
optional.description: Indicates whether to mark targeted notifications as read (`true`) or unread (`false`). Defaults to `true` (mark as read) if not provided.

optional.name: last_read_at
optional.description: If provided, only notifications updated at or before this timestamp are affected. If omitted, all current notifications are targeted.

title: Mark pull request ready for review
description: Marks a draft pull request as ready for review using GitHub GraphQL API, transitioning it from draft to reviewable state. Use this action when a draft pull request has reached a stage where it is ready for team review and can potentially be merged. This action cannot be used on pull requests that are already marked as ready for review.

required.name: pull_request_id
required.description: The global Node ID of the pull request to mark as ready for review (e.g., 'PR_kwDOABCDEFGHIJK'). This is the GraphQL ID, not the numeric pull request number. You can obtain this ID from the 'node_id' field when listing or getting pull requests.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. Used to ensure idempotency of mutations and track the request.

title: Mark repository notifications as read
description: Marks notifications in a repository as read; if 'last_read_at' is specified, notifications updated after this timestamp are not marked as read.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the account owning the repository (case-insensitive).

optional.name: last_read_at
optional.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`). If provided, notifications updated *after* this time will NOT be marked as read. If omitted, all notifications in the repository are marked as read. Defaults to the current time.

title: Merge a branch
description: Merges a head branch or commit SHA into a base branch in a repository; fails if there are merge conflicts requiring manual resolution.

required.name: base
required.description: The name of the branch to merge the `head` branch into.

required.name: head
required.description: Source branch name or full commit SHA to merge into the `base` branch.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Username or organization name of the repository owner. Not case-sensitive.

optional.name: commit_message
optional.description: Commit message for the merge. If omitted, GitHub uses a default message.

title: Merge a pull request
description: Merges an open and mergeable pull request in a repository. A 405 error can occur for multiple reasons: (1) The PR is still in draft mode - convert it to ready-for-review first using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST. (2) Branch protection rules are not satisfied - check for required approving reviews, status checks, or other repository rules that must be met before merging. (3) The base branch has been modified since the PR was last synced - update the PR branch first using GITHUB_UPDATE_A_PULL_REQUEST_BRANCH.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Repository owner's username. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: The unique number identifying the pull request. The PR must be mergeable: not a draft, and all branch protection rules (required reviews, status checks, etc.) must be satisfied.

optional.name: sha
optional.description: SHA of the pull request's head commit. Must match for merge to succeed, ensuring PR hasn't changed since review.

optional.name: commit_title
optional.description: Title for the merge commit message.

optional.name: merge_method
optional.description: Merge strategy: 'merge', 'squash', or 'rebase'. Defaults to repository's setting if unspecified.

optional.name: commit_message
optional.description: Additional details for the merge commit message.

title: Ping an organization webhook
description: Sends a 'ping' event to a specified, existing organization webhook to test its configuration and ensure it correctly receives events.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: hook_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the webhook. This ID can be found in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.

title: Ping a repository webhook
description: Pings an existing webhook on a repository to test its configuration and reachability by GitHub.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: hook_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the hook. You can find this value in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.

title: Privately report a security vulnerability
description: Privately reports a security vulnerability to a repository's maintainers. IMPORTANT: You cannot report vulnerabilities to repositories you own - this API is for third-party security researchers to report to other repositories. The target repository must have private vulnerability reporting enabled. Specify EITHER `severity` OR `cvss_vector_string`, but not both.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: summary
required.description: A short, descriptive summary of the security vulnerability.

required.name: description
required.description: A detailed explanation of the security vulnerability, its impact, and potential mitigations.

optional.name: cwe_ids
optional.description: A list of Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) identifiers relevant to the vulnerability.

optional.name: severity
optional.description: The advisory's severity level. Mutually exclusive with `cvss_vector_string`.

optional.name: vulnerabilities
optional.description: JSON string representing a list of vulnerability objects detailing the affected packages or products. Each object should specify the package's ecosystem and name, the vulnerable version range, and optionally, patched versions and vulnerable functions.

optional.name: cvss_vector_string
optional.description: The CVSS vector string for advisory severity. Mutually exclusive with `severity`.

optional.name: start_private_fork
optional.description: Whether to create a temporary private fork to collaborate on a fix for the reported vulnerability.

title: Publish Sponsors Tier (GraphQL)
description: Tool to publish a draft GitHub Sponsors tier using GraphQL. Use when you need to make a draft sponsors tier visible to potential sponsors. The tier must already exist in draft status.

required.name: tier_id
required.description: The global Relay ID of the draft sponsors tier to publish. Must be a tier that is currently in draft status.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. Used to track requests.

title: Redeliver a delivery for an organization webhook
description: Redelivers a specific webhook delivery for a webhook within an organization, to resend an event that previously failed or was not processed.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: hook_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the webhook. This ID can be found in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery or by listing webhooks for an organization.

required.name: delivery_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the specific webhook delivery to be redelivered. This ID is typically obtained from the `X-GitHub-Delivery` header of the original delivery attempt or by listing deliveries for a webhook.

title: Redeliver a delivery for a repository webhook
description: Redelivers a specific, previously made webhook delivery (`delivery_id`) for a repository's webhook (`hook_id`).

required.name: repo
required.description: The repository name, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: The account username that owns the repository (not case-sensitive).

required.name: hook_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the webhook (e.g., from `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header or by listing repository webhooks).

required.name: delivery_id
required.description: Unique identifier of a specific past delivery for the webhook (obtainable by listing deliveries for that webhook).

title: Remove a custom property for an organization
description: Deletes a custom property, specified by `custom_property_name`, from an existing organization (`org`) for which the property is currently defined, preventing its future assignment to repositories.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: custom_property_name
required.description: The name of the custom property to remove. This name is case sensitive.

title: Remove a label from an issue
description: Removes a label currently applied to a specific issue in a repository.

required.name: name
required.description: The name of the label to remove from the issue. Emoji reactions will not be removed and names with spaces or special characters must be URL-encoded.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The number that identifies the issue.

title: Remove all labels from an issue
description: Removes all labels from a specified issue in a GitHub repository; this operation is idempotent.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the '.git' extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The unique number that identifies the issue from which all labels will be removed.

title: Remove all organization roles for a team
description: Revokes all organization roles for a team in an organization; this is destructive and succeeds even if the team initially has no roles.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name. Team slugs are typically all lowercase and replace spaces with hyphens.

title: Remove all organization roles for a user
description: Revokes all assigned organization-level roles from a specified user (who must be a member of the organization) within a GitHub organization, without removing the user from the organization or affecting repository-specific roles.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: username
required.description: The handle for the GitHub user account.

title: Remove an organization member
description: Removes a member from a GitHub organization. This action permanently removes a user's membership from the specified organization, revoking their access to all organization resources, repositories, and teams. Requirements: - The authenticated user must be an organization owner - The target user must currently be a member of the organization Note: This action cannot be used to remove the last owner of an organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name (case-insensitive). Must be an organization where the authenticated user has owner permissions.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the member to remove. The user must currently be a member of the organization.

title: Remove an organization role from a team
description: Revokes an organization role that a team currently possesses within an organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This value is not case sensitive.

required.name: role_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the organization role to be removed from the team.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug (short name) of the team.

title: Remove an organization role from a user
description: Removes a custom organization role from a user within a GitHub organization, provided the organization exists, the user is a member, and the role_id corresponds to a valid custom role in that organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The GitHub organization's name (not case-sensitive).

required.name: role_id
required.description: Unique ID of the organization role to be removed. Use the 'Get all organization roles' action to retrieve valid role IDs.

required.name: username
required.description: GitHub username of the user.

title: Remove app access restrictions
description: Removes all GitHub App access restrictions from a protected branch in a repository; the branch must have protection rules configured, and this action does not alter user or team restrictions.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch from which all app access restrictions will be removed. Wildcard characters are not supported; for branches with wildcards, please use the GraphQL API.

title: Remove a project from a team
description: Removes a project from a team within an organization; this action requires the project to be currently associated with the team.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name (URL-friendly version, e.g., 'justice-league').

required.name: project_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the project to be removed from the team.

title: Remove a repository collaborator
description: Removes a collaborator from a specified GitHub repository, provided the repository exists and the user is an existing collaborator.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the collaborator to remove.

title: Remove a repository from an app installation
description: Removes a repository from a GitHub App installation for the authenticated user, given a valid `installation_id` and the `repository_id` of a repository currently linked to that installation; this operation is idempotent.

required.name: repository_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the repository to be removed from the installation.

required.name: installation_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the GitHub App installation from which to remove the repository.

title: Remove a repository from a team
description: Disassociates a repository from a team; team members may lose access permissions, but the repository and team are not deleted.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization where the team and repository exist. This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the '.git' extension. This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The URL-friendly identifier (slug) for the team. Team slugs are typically all lowercase with hyphens instead of spaces (e.g., 'justice-league' for 'Justice League').

title: Remove a selected repository from a user secret
description: Removes a selected repository's access to a user's Codespaces secret; the secret must exist and the repository must have previously been granted access.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: Name of the user's Codespaces secret from which repository access will be revoked.

required.name: repository_id
required.description: The unique integer identifier of the repository that will lose access to the specified Codespaces secret.

title: Remove assignees from an issue
description: Removes specified assignees from a GitHub issue; requires push access, and invalid removal attempts are silently ignored.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, excluding the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The unique number that identifies the issue within the repository.

optional.name: assignees
optional.description: Usernames to unassign from the issue. Note: Requires push access to the repository; attempts to remove users without permission or those not currently assigned are silently ignored.

title: Remove custom label from repo runner
description: Removes a custom label from a repository's self-hosted runner; this operation is idempotent.

required.name: name
required.description: Name of the custom label to remove from the self-hosted runner. Note: only custom labels can be removed; read-only system labels (like 'self-hosted', 'linux', 'x64') cannot be removed.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

required.name: runner_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner. Get this from listing runners for the repository.

title: Remove custom label from self hosted runner
description: Removes a currently assigned custom label (`name`) from a self-hosted runner (`runner_id`) in an organization (`org`). This action allows the organization to manage the labels associated with their runners effectively.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: name
required.description: The name of the custom label to remove from the self-hosted runner.

required.name: runner_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner.

title: Remove custom labels from self hosted repo runner
description: Removes all custom labels from a self-hosted runner registered at the repository level, leaving only its default labels and any labels inherited from its runner group or organization.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: runner_id
required.description: Unique identifier (ID) of the self-hosted runner.

title: Remove interaction restrictions for an organization
description: Removes all interaction restrictions from public repositories in the specified GitHub organization, allowing all users to resume interactions.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

title: Remove interaction restrictions for a repository
description: Removes all interaction restrictions for a repository, enabling all users to comment, open issues, and create pull requests by lifting any existing temporary interaction limits.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension; case-insensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Username or organization name of the repository owner; case-insensitive.

title: Remove org dev env secret by name
description: Deletes a GitHub Codespaces secret from an organization by its name; this operation is idempotent.

required.name: org
required.description: Name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive).

required.name: secret_name
required.description: Name of the Codespaces secret to remove.

title: Remove org secret by name
description: Permanently removes a specific Dependabot secret, by its `secret_name`, from the GitHub `org`, making it unavailable to Dependabot for that organization.

required.name: org
required.description: GitHub organization name (case-insensitive).

required.name: secret_name
required.description: Dependabot secret name to remove from the organization.

title: Remove outside collaborator from an organization
description: Removes a user, who must be an outside collaborator, from the specified GitHub organization, revoking their access to all its repositories.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the outside collaborator to remove.

title: Remove public org membership
description: Removes the authenticated user's public organization membership, making it private. The user remains a member of the organization but their membership is no longer publicly visible. This operation is idempotent - calling it when the membership is already private will succeed.

required.name: org
required.description: Name of the GitHub organization (case-insensitive). The authenticated user must be a member of this organization.

required.name: username
required.description: GitHub username of the authenticated user. Must match the currently authenticated user - you can only modify your own public membership status.

title: Remove user public repo interaction restrictions
description: Removes all interaction restrictions (limitations on comments, issues, or pull requests) from all public repositories owned by the authenticated user.

title: Remove repository from organization dev environment secret
description: Removes a repository's access to an organization-level Codespaces secret, if it was previously granted.

required.name: org
required.description: The GitHub organization name (not case-sensitive).

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The Codespaces secret name.

required.name: repository_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the repository.

title: Remove selected repo from org secret
description: Revokes a specific repository's access to an organization-level Dependabot secret, applicable only when the secret has 'selected' visibility and the specified repository currently has access.

required.name: org
required.description: Name of the organization (not case-sensitive).

required.name: secret_name
required.description: Name of the Dependabot secret.

required.name: repository_id
required.description: Unique numeric ID of the repository (not the repository name).

title: Remove requested reviewers from a pull request
description: Removes currently assigned user logins and/or team slugs from a GitHub pull request's list of requested reviewers.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the repository owner (not case-sensitive).

required.name: reviewers
required.description: GitHub user `login`s for removal. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be specified.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: Number of the pull request.

required.name: team_reviewers
required.description: GitHub team `slug`s (URL-friendly names) for removal. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be specified.

title: Remove review request
description: Removes requested reviewers from a pull request. Use this action when you need to cancel a review request that was previously sent to users or teams. Only users with push access to the repository can remove review requests.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: reviewers
required.description: An array of user logins that will be removed from the review request.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: The number that identifies the pull request.

optional.name: team_reviewers
optional.description: An array of team slugs that will be removed from the review request.

title: Remove selected repository from an organization secret
description: Removes a specific repository's access to an organization-level secret; the repository must have been previously granted access to this secret.

required.name: org
required.description: Organization name (case-insensitive).

required.name: secret_name
required.description: Name of the organization secret.

required.name: repository_id
required.description: Repository ID to remove from the secret's access.

title: Remove selected repository from an organization variable
description: Removes a repository's access to an organization variable that has 'selected' visibility. This endpoint removes a specific repository from an organization variable's access list. The variable must have its visibility set to 'selected' for this operation to work. Returns a 409 Conflict error if the variable visibility is not 'selected'.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization's name (case-insensitive).

required.name: name
required.description: Name of the organization variable.

required.name: repository_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the repository.

title: Remove status check contexts
description: Removes specified status check contexts from a protected branch's required status checks. This action removes the specified status check contexts from the existing list of required status checks for a protected branch. The branch must already have branch protection enabled with status checks configured. Note: The 'contexts' parameter is deprecated by GitHub in favor of 'checks' array. For new implementations, consider using update_status_check_protection with the 'checks' parameter instead.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch. Wildcard characters are not allowed. To use wildcard characters in branch names, refer to the GraphQL API documentation.

required.name: contexts
required.description: The status check contexts to remove from the protected branch. These are the names of CI/CD jobs or other checks that should no longer be required before merging. Can be provided as a single string or a list of strings. Examples: 'ci/test', 'linter', 'continuous-integration/travis-ci'.

title: Remove status check protection
description: Removes status check protection from a branch, disabling required status checks for merging pull requests; will only have an effect if status check protection is currently configured on the branch.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner (username or organization) of the repository; not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: Name of the branch; wildcard characters are not allowed.

title: Remove team access restrictions
description: Removes specified teams from push access to a protected branch. This action removes teams from the list of teams with push access to a protected branch. Removing a team will also remove push access for any child teams. Prerequisites: - The repository must be owned by an organization (not a personal account) - The branch must have protection rules enabled - The branch protection must have restrictions configured - The teams must currently have push access to the branch

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The organization name that owns the repository. Team access restrictions only work for organization-owned repositories, not personal repositories. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: teams
required.description: The list of team slugs to remove from push access to the protected branch. A team slug is the URL-friendly version of the team name (lowercase, hyphens instead of spaces). Removing a team will also remove push access for any child teams. This removes teams from the existing list (does not replace the entire list).

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the protected branch to remove team restrictions from. The branch must already have branch protection enabled with restrictions configured. Wildcard characters are not supported. For wildcard branch protection, use the GitHub GraphQL API.

title: Remove team membership
description: Tool to remove team membership for a user in an organization. Use when you need to revoke a user's membership from a specific team. This action is irreversible — the user must be explicitly re-added if you want to restore their team membership. Note that if team synchronization is set up, this operation may fail with a 403 Forbidden error.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: username
required.description: The handle for the GitHub user account.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name.

title: Remove team membership for a user
description: Removes a user from a specific team within an organization. This action requires admin:org scope permissions. It will fail if: - Team synchronization with an Identity Provider (IdP) is enabled (403 Forbidden) - The organization, team, or user membership doesn't exist (404 Not Found) - You don't have sufficient permissions to manage team memberships (403 Forbidden) Note: If the removed user was the last member and the team is not nested, the team may be deleted automatically.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization that owns the team. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the user to remove from the team. Must be an exact match of the user's login handle.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The URL-friendly identifier (slug) of the team. This is the hyphenated, lowercase version of the team name as it appears in the team's URL (e.g., 'justice-league' for a team named 'Justice League').

title: Remove user access restrictions
description: Removes specified users from the list of people allowed to push to a protected branch. Important notes: - This action only works on organization-owned repositories (not personal repos) - The branch must have protection rules with push restrictions enabled - Users being removed must currently have push access to the branch - The combined total of users, apps, and teams is limited to 100 items

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. Must be an organization name (user access restrictions only work on organization repositories). Not case-sensitive.

required.name: users
required.description: The list of user logins to remove from push access to the protected branch. These users will no longer be able to push directly to this branch. The combined total of users, apps, and teams with restrictions is limited to 100 items.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch from which to remove user access restrictions. Wildcard characters (e.g., '*') are not allowed. Use the GitHub GraphQL API for wildcard branch patterns.

title: Remove users from codespaces access for an organization
description: Removes selected users from GitHub Codespaces billing access for an existing organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: selected_usernames
required.description: A list of GitHub usernames, typically organization members. After removal, the organization will no longer be billed for Codespaces created by these users.

title: Rename a branch
description: Renames an existing branch in a GitHub repository; the new name must be unique and adhere to GitHub's naming conventions, and the current branch name cannot contain wildcard characters.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The current name of the branch. Wildcard characters (e.g., `*`) are not allowed.

required.name: new_name
required.description: The new name for the branch. Must be unique and adhere to GitHub's branch naming conventions (e.g., no spaces, '..', or leading/trailing slashes).

title: Render a markdown document
description: Renders Markdown to HTML; for 'gfm' mode, provide 'context' (owner/repo) to correctly link issues, pull requests, and user mentions.

required.name: text
required.description: The Markdown string to convert to HTML.

optional.name: mode
optional.description: Rendering mode: 'markdown' for standard Markdown or 'gfm' for GitHub Flavored Markdown.

optional.name: context
optional.description: The repository context (e.g., 'owner/repo') used when `mode` is 'gfm'.

title: Render Markdown (Raw Mode)
description: Tool to render raw Markdown text to HTML using GitHub's markdown API. Use when you need to convert plain Markdown content to HTML without GitHub-specific features like issue references or @mentions.

required.name: markdown_content
required.description: The raw Markdown text to render as HTML. This can include any valid Markdown syntax like headers, lists, links, bold/italic text, code blocks, etc.

title: Reopen an issue
description: Reopens a closed GitHub issue by changing its state to 'open' with state_reason 'reopened'. Use this action when you need to reopen a previously closed issue that requires further attention or work. Only users with push access to the repository can reopen issues.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the .git extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The number that identifies the issue.

title: Reopen Pull Request
description: Reopens a previously closed pull request by setting its state to 'open'. This restores the pull request to an active state where it can be reviewed, commented on, and merged. Use this action when you need to reactivate a closed pull request that was closed prematurely or needs to be reconsidered for merging.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the .git extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: The number that identifies the pull request.

title: Replace all repository topics
description: Replaces all topics of a repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This is case-insensitive.

required.name: names
required.description: A list of topic names to replace the current set of topics for the repository. Provide one or more topics to set them. To remove all topics, pass an empty list (`[]`). Note: Topic names cannot contain uppercase letters and are limited to 25 characters.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This is case-insensitive.

title: Replace org secret visibility to selected
description: Replaces the list of repositories that can access a Dependabot organization secret when the secret's visibility is already set to 'selected'.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This parameter is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: Name of the Dependabot secret (alphanumeric characters and underscores only, no spaces allowed).

required.name: selected_repository_ids
required.description: Array of repository IDs that can access this organization Dependabot secret. This list completely replaces any current repository associations. For incremental changes (add/remove individual repos), use dedicated add/remove repository secret actions instead.

title: Replace repository access for an org Codespaces secret
description: Replaces the list of repositories that can access an organization-level Codespaces secret. This operation completely replaces the existing list of repositories with the provided list. The secret must already have its visibility set to 'selected' for this operation to succeed. Use this when you want to set an exact list of repositories that should have access. Prerequisites: - The organization must exist and you must have admin:org scope - The Codespaces secret must already exist in the organization - The secret's visibility must be set to 'selected' (not 'all' or 'private') Returns HTTP 204 No Content on success, 404 if secret/org not found, 409 if visibility is not 'selected'.

required.name: org
required.description: The GitHub organization name (case-insensitive).

required.name: secret_name
required.description: Name of the development environment secret for which repository access is being configured.

required.name: selected_repository_ids
required.description: Array of repository IDs that can access the organization Codespaces secret. This completely replaces any existing list of repositories. Note: The secret's visibility must already be set to 'selected' (not 'all' or 'private') for this operation to succeed; otherwise, a 409 Conflict error is returned.

title: Request a github pages build
description: Manually triggers a GitHub Pages build for a repository if GitHub Pages is enabled, useful for deployments not automatically built or for retrying failed builds.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

title: Request reviewers for a pull request
description: Requests reviewers for a specific pull request identified by owner, repository, and pull request number. Use this action when you need to add individual users or teams as reviewers to an existing pull request. At least one of reviewers (individual users) or team_reviewers (teams) must be provided.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (username or organization name). Not case sensitive.

required.name: reviewers
required.description: GitHub user login strings (usernames) to request reviews from. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be provided.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: Number identifying the pull request.

required.name: team_reviewers
required.description: GitHub team slug strings (e.g., 'justice-league') to request reviews from. Slugs are typically lowercase and use hyphens for spaces. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be provided.

title: Add reviewers to a specific pull request
description: Adds reviewers to a specific pull request identified by owner, repo, and pull_number. This is NOT a search action - it operates on an already-known PR number. Requires `owner`, `repo`, `pull_number`, and at least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers`.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (username or organization name); not case sensitive.

required.name: reviewers
required.description: GitHub user `login` strings (usernames) to request reviews from. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be provided.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: Number identifying the pull request.

required.name: team_reviewers
required.description: GitHub team `slug` strings (e.g., 'justice-league') to request reviews from. Slugs are typically lowercase and use hyphens for spaces. At least one of `reviewers` or `team_reviewers` must be provided.

title: Rerequest a check run
description: Triggers a re-run of a specific check run in a GitHub repository, resetting its status to 'queued', clearing its conclusion, and triggering the `check_run` webhook with `rerequested` action. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires GitHub App authentication with 'checks:write' permission. The check run can ONLY be re-requested by the same GitHub App that originally created it. OAuth tokens and personal access tokens (PAT) cannot use this endpoint.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: check_run_id
required.description: The unique numerical identifier of the check run to be re-requested. Must be a check run created by the same GitHub App making the request.

title: Rerequest a check suite
description: Triggers a new run of an existing check suite within a repository, resetting its status to 'queued', clearing its conclusion, and triggering the `check_suite` webhook with `rerequested` action. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires GitHub App authentication with 'checks:write' permission. OAuth tokens and classic personal access tokens (PAT) cannot use this endpoint. Only GitHub App user access tokens, GitHub App installation access tokens, or fine-grained personal access tokens with checks:write permission are supported.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name). This field is case-insensitive.

required.name: check_suite_id
required.description: The unique numerical identifier of the check suite to be re-requested. You can obtain this from the list_check_suites_for_a_git_reference endpoint or from a workflow run.

title: Re-run a job from a workflow run
description: Re-runs a specific job and any dependent jobs from a GitHub Actions workflow run in the specified repository, optionally enabling debug logging.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: job_id
required.description: The unique numerical identifier of the job to be re-run. This ID can be obtained by listing jobs for a workflow run.

optional.name: enable_debug_logging
optional.description: If `true`, enables additional debug logging for the re-run of the job. Defaults to `false` if not provided.

title: Rerun a workflow
description: Re-runs a specific GitHub Actions workflow run identified by its owner, repository, and run ID, optionally enabling debug logging.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository (without the `.git` extension) where the workflow run exists (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository where the workflow run exists (not case-sensitive).

required.name: run_id
required.description: Unique ID of the workflow run to re-execute.

optional.name: enable_debug_logging
optional.description: Set to `true` to enable diagnostic logging for the re-run, helpful for troubleshooting.

title: Rerun failed jobs from a workflow run
description: Re-runs all failed jobs and their dependent jobs from a specified workflow run if the run contains previously failed jobs.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name); not case-sensitive.

required.name: run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run.

optional.name: enable_debug_logging
optional.description: Set to `true` to enable extensive debug logging for the re-run, providing additional logs to aid in diagnosing issues.

title: Reset a token
description: Invalidates the provided OAuth `access_token` and generates a new one for the GitHub OAuth App identified by `client_id`. Used for token rotation when a token may be compromised or for regular security maintenance. Note: This endpoint requires the OAuth App owner's credentials (client_id/client_secret for Basic Auth).

required.name: client_id
required.description: The client ID of the GitHub OAuth App.

required.name: access_token
required.description: The existing OAuth access token that needs to be reset. This token will be invalidated and replaced by a new one.

title: Restore a package for an organization
description: Restores a package in an organization, provided it was deleted within the last 30 days.

required.name: org
required.description: Name of the GitHub organization that owns the package (case-insensitive).

required.name: package_name
required.description: Unique name of the package to be restored.

required.name: package_type
required.description: Type of the package. Gradle packages use `maven`. Docker images in `ghcr.io` use `container`; `docker` finds images from `docker.pkg.github.com`, even if migrated.

optional.name: token
optional.description: Optional token for restoring private packages or specific versions requiring special permissions.

title: Restore a package for a user
description: Restores a user-owned package previously deleted from GitHub Packages, if restorable under GitHub's data retention policy (typically within 30 days of deletion).

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the account that owns the deleted package.

required.name: package_name
required.description: The unique name of the deleted package to restore.

required.name: package_type
required.description: The type of GitHub package registry. Supported values: npm, maven, rubygems, docker, nuget, container. Use `maven` for Gradle packages. `docker` can be used for images migrated from `docker.pkg.github.com` to the Container registry (`ghcr.io`), while `container` is for images originally pushed to `ghcr.io`.

optional.name: token
optional.description: Optional package version token. Only required when restoring packages with versions that have more than 50,000 downloads.

title: Restore a package for the authenticated user
description: Restores a package deleted by the authenticated user within the last 30 days, if its namespace and version are still available.

required.name: package_name
required.description: The unique name of the package to be restored within its namespace and type.

required.name: package_type
required.description: The type of the package to be restored, specifying its ecosystem. For example, `npm` for Node.js packages, `maven` for Java packages. Special cases: packages in GitHub's Gradle registry use the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) use the type `container`. The `docker` type can be used to find images originally pushed to GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if they have been migrated to the Container registry.

optional.name: token
optional.description: Optional token to identify a specific package version to restore, useful if multiple versions were deleted. If omitted, the most recently deleted version is typically restored.

title: Restore a package version for the authenticated user
description: Restores a package version that was deleted by the authenticated user within the last 30 days.

required.name: package_name
required.description: Name of the package.

required.name: package_type
required.description: Specifies the package type. Use `maven` for GitHub's Gradle registry. Use `container` for images in GitHub's Container registry (ghcr.io). `docker` can be used for images previously in GitHub's Docker registry (docker.pkg.github.com), even if migrated.

required.name: package_version_id
required.description: Unique ID of the package version to restore.

title: Restore package version for an organization
description: Restores a package version for an organization, provided it was deleted within the last 30 days.

required.name: org
required.description: Organization name (case-insensitive).

required.name: package_name
required.description: Unique name of the package.

required.name: package_type
required.description: The type of package. Supported types include "npm", "maven", "rubygems", "docker", "nuget", and "container". Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry use the `maven` type. Docker images in GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) use the `container` type. The `docker` type can be used for images previously in GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if migrated to the Container registry.

required.name: package_version_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the package version.

title: Restore package version for a user
description: Restores a specific, user-owned package version if it was deleted within the last 30 days and its original namespace and version name are still available.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the package owner.

required.name: package_name
required.description: The name of the package.

required.name: package_type
required.description: Specifies the package type. Packages in GitHub's Gradle registry have the type `maven`. Docker images pushed to GitHub's Container registry (`ghcr.io`) have the type `container`. Use `docker` for images from GitHub's Docker registry (`docker.pkg.github.com`), even if migrated to the Container registry.

required.name: package_version_id
required.description: The unique numeric identifier of the package version to be restored. Obtain this by first listing package versions using 'list_package_versions_for_a_package_owned_by_a_user'.

title: Retire Sponsors Tier
description: Tool to retire a published payment tier from your GitHub Sponsors profile using GraphQL. Use when you need to prevent a tier from being used for new sponsorships. Existing sponsors at this tier remain unaffected.

required.name: tier_id
required.description: The global node ID of the sponsors tier to retire (e.g., 'ST_kwDOCNqc1s4ACOVb'). Once retired, this tier cannot be used to start new sponsorships, but existing sponsors at this tier are unaffected.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. Used to ensure idempotency of mutations and track request origin.

title: Review access with personal token
description: Approves or denies a pending fine-grained personal access token request for organization resources; must be performed by a GitHub App.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: action
required.description: The action to take on the personal access token request. Must be 'approve' to approve the request or 'deny' to deny it.

required.name: pat_request_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the pending fine-grained personal access token request that needs to be reviewed.

optional.name: reason
optional.description: An optional comment explaining the reason for approving or denying the request. Maximum length is 1024 characters.

title: Review Custom Deployment Rules For Workflow Run
description: Approves or rejects pending custom deployment protection rules for a workflow run. This endpoint allows GitHub Apps to review their own pending custom deployment protection rules for a specific workflow run. The review can either approve (allowing the deployment to proceed) or reject (blocking the deployment). **Important notes:** - GitHub Apps can only review their own custom deployment protection rules - This endpoint requires GitHub App installation access tokens with Deployments permission (write) - Custom deployment protection rules are available in public repos for all plans; for private/internal repos, GitHub Enterprise is required - Returns 204 No Content on success

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Repository owner's username or organization name (case-insensitive).

required.name: state
required.description: The review decision: 'approved' to allow the deployment or 'rejected' to block it.

required.name: run_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the workflow run.

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the deployment environment to review (e.g., 'production', 'staging').

optional.name: comment
optional.description: Optional comment to include with the review decision.

title: Review pending deployments for a workflow run
description: Approves or rejects pending deployments for a specific workflow run that are in a 'waiting' state within specified, configured environments.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: state
required.description: State to apply to the pending deployments.

required.name: run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run.

required.name: comment
required.description: Comment to include with the review decision.

required.name: environment_ids
required.description: Environments targeted by the review; they must be configured for the repository and be part of the pending deployments for this run.

title: Review PAT Requests in Bulk
description: Approves or denies multiple fine-grained personal access token requests for an organization in bulk. This endpoint processes multiple PAT request approvals or denials in a single API call. All specified pat_request_ids must refer to currently pending requests. Important: This endpoint can ONLY be called by GitHub Apps with the 'organization_personal_access_token_requests:write' permission. It cannot be called with personal access tokens or OAuth apps. On success, returns HTTP 202 Accepted with an empty body.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name where the token requests are pending. Case-insensitive.

required.name: action
required.description: The action to perform on the specified token requests. Use 'approve' to grant access or 'deny' to reject the requests.

required.name: pat_request_ids
required.description: List of unique identifiers for the fine-grained personal access token requests to review. Must contain between 1 and 100 request IDs. Get these IDs from the 'List requests to access organization resources' endpoint.

optional.name: reason
optional.description: Optional reason for the decision. Maximum 1024 characters. This reason is stored and may be visible to the requester.

title: Revoke an installation access token
description: Revokes the GitHub App's current installation access token, immediately invalidating it for API authentication. IMPORTANT: This endpoint requires a GitHub App installation access token (ghs_* prefix) for authentication. OAuth tokens (gho_*) or personal access tokens are not supported and will result in a 403 Forbidden error. After successful revocation, the token becomes permanently invalid and cannot be used for any subsequent API calls. To continue API operations, a new installation access token must be generated.

title: Run GraphQL Query
description: Tool to run an arbitrary GitHub GraphQL v4 query or mutation. Use when fetching multiple datasets in one batch. Cost-based rate limit: ~5,000 points/hour; keep field selections narrow, avoid deep nesting, and include rateLimit in responses to monitor quota. Responses are nested under data.data (e.g., data.data.repository.vulnerabilityAlerts); always inspect the errors array even on HTTP 200, as partial failures embed there. Paginate by looping on pageInfo.hasNextPage and advancing with pageInfo.endCursor. Search results cap at ~1,000 items per query; split by label, date range, or repository for full coverage. Use ProjectV2 nodes, not Classic Projects (deprecated). Parallel mutations (e.g., addProjectV2ItemById) can trigger transient conflicts; use sequential execution.

required.name: query
required.description: GraphQL query or mutation string. Must comply with GitHub's GraphQL v4 schema.

optional.name: variables
optional.description: JSON object mapping variable names to values for use in the query.

title: Run GraphQL Relay Query
description: Tool to run a GitHub GraphQL relay query. The relay field is a workaround for re-exposing the root query object. Use when you need to access root query fields through the relay context.

required.name: query
required.description: GraphQL query string to execute within the relay context. Must comply with GitHub's GraphQL v4 schema. The relay field re-exposes the root Query object, allowing you to nest any valid root query fields.

optional.name: variables
optional.description: JSON object mapping variable names to values for use in the query. Optional - omit if the query has no variables.

title: Search code
