description: Searches code file contents and paths on the default branch of GitHub repositories using a query string; searches only files under 384KB, returns max 1000 results by best match, and is optimized for precision.

required.name: q
required.description: Code search query, including keywords and qualifiers (e.g., `language:python`, `user:octocat`, `repo:owner/repo`). For full syntax and qualifiers, see GitHub docs: [Constructing a search query](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#constructing-a-search-query) and [code search qualifiers](https://docs.github.com/search-github/searching-on-github/searching-code).

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number for results. For pagination details, see GitHub docs: [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

optional.name: sort
optional.description: DEPRECATED. Valid: 'indexed' (sorts by last indexed time) or 'updated' (sorts by last updated time). If unspecified, results sorted by best match. Docs: [ranking search results](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#ranking-search-results).

optional.name: order
optional.description: DEPRECATED. Order ('asc' or 'desc') for results; effective only if `sort` is specified. Docs: [ranking search results](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#ranking-search-results).

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Results per page (max 100). For pagination details, see GitHub docs: [Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api).

title: Search code (all pages)
description: Tool to search code across multiple pages using GitHub's code search API. Use when single-page searches may miss matches and you need a full or capped result set. GitHub caps results at ~1,000 total items regardless of pagination; results for broad queries may be silently truncated. Only the default branch is indexed, and very large files may be excluded — treat results as potentially partial. Rate limit: ~30 requests/minute; honor `Retry-After` on 403/429 responses.

required.name: q
required.description: The search query string for code search. **IMPORTANT**: While GitHub's documentation mentions boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) support, the REST API still uses older syntax that frequently rejects queries with operators or parentheses (ERROR_TYPE_QUERY_PARSING_FATAL). For reliable searches, avoid boolean operators and parentheses. Supports qualifiers: `language:`, `repo:`, `path:`, `extension:`, `user:`, `org:`, `in:file`. Multiple terms use implicit AND: `hello world` finds both. Quote exact phrases: `"exact phrase"`. For complex boolean logic, use multiple separate API calls or the GitHub web interface.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number to start retrieval (min 1).

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Sort field: only 'indexed' is valid (sort by last indexed time).

optional.name: limit
optional.description: Optional cap on total number of items to retrieve across pages (min 1).

optional.name: order
optional.description: Sort order for results: 'asc' or 'desc'. Only effective when `sort` is provided.

optional.name: accept
optional.description: Custom Accept header for media type (e.g., `application/vnd.github.text-match+json` to include text match metadata).

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (min 1, max 100).

title: Search commits
description: Finds commits on GitHub using a query string (q) supporting keywords and qualifiers, with options for sorting and pagination.

required.name: q
required.description: Search query with at least one text keyword plus optional qualifiers. GitHub requires actual search text (commit message keywords) - qualifiers alone are not allowed. Common qualifiers: 'repo:owner/name', 'author:username', 'committer:username', 'author-date:YYYY-MM-DD' or 'author-date:>YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD', 'committer-date:YYYY-MM-DD', 'merge:true/false', 'hash:HASH', 'parent:HASH', 'tree:HASH'. IMPORTANT: The 'hash:' qualifier requires a full 40-character hexadecimal commit hash (e.g., 'hash:e5bd3914e2e596debea16f433f57875b5b90bcd6'). Do NOT use branch names, tag names, or short refs with 'hash:' - use 'repo:owner/name' with other filters to search commits on a specific branch.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results to retrieve.

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Sorts results by 'author-date' or 'committer-date'. Use separately with the 'order' parameter (e.g., sort='committer-date' with order='desc'). Do not combine them into a single value. If unspecified, GitHub defaults to 'best match' ranking.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Sort order: 'desc' (newest first) or 'asc' (oldest first). Use with the 'sort' parameter to control direction (e.g., sort='committer-date' with order='desc').

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100).

title: Search commits by author across repos
description: Searches commits across GitHub using the Search API (e.g., by author/email/org/date range) without per-repo scanning. Use when you need to find commits by author, committer email, organization, or date ranges across multiple repositories. This avoids the need to list commits per repository and prevents 409 errors on empty repos.

required.name: q
required.description: GitHub search query for commits. IMPORTANT: Must include search text (keywords) in addition to qualifiers. Qualifier-only queries are not allowed by the GitHub API. Supports qualifiers like author:, committer-email:, org:, repo:, author-date:, committer-date:, merge:, hash:, parent:, tree:, is:public/private. Examples: 'fix author:octocat', 'bug repo:owner/repo', 'update author:octocat author-date:>=2025-01-01'. If only qualifiers are provided, a wildcard search term will be automatically added.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of results to fetch.

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Sort options for commit search.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Order options for search results.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100).

optional.name: composio_execution_message
optional.description: Message about any automatic modifications made to the input

title: GitHub GraphQL Search
description: Tool to perform GitHub GraphQL searches across issues, pull requests, repositories, users, and discussions. Returns up to 1,000 results with cursor-based pagination. Use when you need structured search results with specific fields.

required.name: type
required.description: The type of resource to search. Determines the structure of returned results.

required.name: query
required.description: The search query string using GitHub search syntax. Supports qualifiers like 'repo:', 'org:', 'user:', 'is:open', 'is:closed', 'label:', etc. For issues/PRs, use 'is:issue' or 'is:pr'. For repositories, search by name, description, or topics. Maximum 1,000 results can be retrieved across all pages.

optional.name: after
optional.description: Cursor string obtained from pageInfo.endCursor in a previous response. Returns results after this cursor for pagination.

optional.name: first
optional.description: Number of results to return (1-100). Returns the first N elements from the result set. Use with 'after' parameter for pagination.

title: Search issues and pull requests
description: Searches GitHub issues and pull requests using a flexible query with qualifiers, sorting, and pagination. Use this action when you need to find issues or pull requests across repositories using search criteria like author, labels, state, milestone, or date ranges. This action searches across all repositories accessible to the authenticated user unless constrained by qualifiers like repo:, user:, or org:.

required.name: q
required.description: Search query string for issues and pull requests. Supports qualifiers: `repo:owner/repo`, `user:username`, `org:orgname`, `author:username`, `assignee:username`, `mentions:username`, `commenter:username`, `involves:username`, `label:labelname`, `milestone:title`, `state:open|closed`, `type:pr|issue`, `is:pr|issue|open|closed|merged|unmerged|locked|unlocked|draft`, `in:title|body|comments`, `created:YYYY-MM-DD`, `updated:YYYY-MM-DD`, `closed:YYYY-MM-DD`, `merged:YYYY-MM-DD`, `no:label|milestone|assignee`, `language:language`, `comments:n`, `reactions:n`, `interactions:n`, `project:number`, `archived:true|false`, `reviewed-by:username`. Use comparison operators (>, <, >=, <=, ..) with numeric/date qualifiers. Multiple terms use implicit AND; quote exact phrases. Example: 'repo:owner/repo is:issue state:open label:bug'

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number to retrieve (min 1).

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Sort options for issue search results.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Order options for search results.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page (min 1, max 100).

title: Search issues and pull requests
description: Searches GitHub for issues and pull requests. Supports keywords, qualifiers (repo:, org:, user:, state:, label:, author:, assignee:, mentions:, etc.), and type filters (is:issue, is:pr). Type filters cannot be used alone - they must be combined with at least one keyword or other qualifier. All other qualifiers work independently. The @me shorthand (e.g., assignee:@me, mentions:@me) is automatically resolved to your username. Logical operators (AND, OR, NOT) are supported but limited to a maximum of 5 operators total per query.

required.name: q
required.description: Search query using GitHub's search syntax. Supports keywords, qualifiers (repo:, org:, user:, state:, label:, author:, assignee:, mentions:, etc.), and type filters (is:issue, is:pr). IMPORTANT: Type filters (is:issue, is:pr) cannot be used alone - they must be combined with at least one keyword or other qualifier. All other qualifiers work independently (e.g., 'state:open', 'label:bug', 'assignee:octocat'). The @me shorthand (e.g., assignee:@me, mentions:@me, author:@me) can be used to reference the authenticated user. Logical operators (AND, OR, NOT) can be used to combine terms (maximum 5 operators total).

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number for results.

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Field for sorting results. GitHub defaults to 'best match' if unspecified.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Order for sorted results (ascending/descending). Effective only if `sort` is also provided.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of results per page.

optional.name: response_detail
optional.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.

title: Search labels
description: Searches for labels within a GitHub repository by keywords in their names or descriptions.

required.name: q
required.description: The search keywords or query to find labels. This endpoint does not accept qualifiers in the query. For more details on query construction, refer to GitHub's documentation on [Constructing a search query](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#constructing-a-search-query).

required.name: repository_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the repository where labels will be searched.

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number of the results to retrieve, starting from 1. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Specifies the field to sort the search results by. Valid options are 'created' or 'updated'. If not provided, results are sorted by best match according to GitHub's default ranking: [best match](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#ranking-search-results).

optional.name: order
optional.description: Determines the sorting order of results, either 'asc' (ascending) or 'desc' (descending). This parameter is only effective when `sort` is also specified. Defaults to 'desc'.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of search results to return per page. The maximum value is 100. For more information, see "[Using pagination in the REST API](https://docs.github.com/rest/using-the-rest-api/using-pagination-in-the-rest-api)."

title: Search repositories
description: Searches GitHub repositories using a flexible query (keywords, qualifiers) with sorting, ordering, and pagination. IMPORTANT: The 'q' parameter (search query) is REQUIRED and must always be provided.

required.name: q
required.description: REQUIRED non-empty search query. Max 5 AND/OR/NOT operators. Qualifiers: `language:LANG`, `stars:N`, `stars:>N`, `forks:N`, `size:N` (KB), `topic:TOPIC`, `license:LICENSE`, `created:DATE`, `pushed:DATE`, `is:public|private`, `archived:true|false`, `in:name|description|readme`, `user:USERNAME`, `org:ORGNAME`. Must use real GitHub usernames/orgs (e.g., `user:octocat`), not placeholders. Queries with logical operators must include at least one plain keyword; `topic:solana OR topic:ethereum` fails, use `solana OR ethereum stars:>100` instead.

optional.name: page
optional.description: The page number for pagination of search results. Defaults to 1. Used in conjunction with `per_page` to fetch subsequent sets of results. See GitHub API documentation for more on pagination.

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Specifies the field to sort the search results by. Options include `stars`, `forks`, `help-wanted-issues`, `updated` (recency of update), or `created` (creation date). If not provided, results are sorted by GitHub's default 'best match' ranking.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Determines the order of search results: `desc` for descending or `asc` for ascending. This parameter is only effective when `sort` is also specified. Defaults to `desc`.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: The number of repository results to return per page. The maximum value is 100. Defaults to 30. See GitHub API documentation for more on pagination.

title: Search topics
description: Finds topics on GitHub using keywords and qualifiers with GitHub's search syntax, supporting pagination.

required.name: q
required.description: Search query string. Supports keywords, qualifiers, and GitHub's search syntax; see [Constructing a search query](https://docs.github.com/rest/search/search#constructing-a-search-query).

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number of the results to retrieve for pagination.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of topic results per page (maximum 100).

title: Search users
description: Searches for users on GitHub by criteria like username, email, location, followers, or repository associations, using a flexible query string `q`.

required.name: q
required.description: Search query string supporting keywords and qualifiers for user attributes (e.g., `username`, `location`, `followers`). See examples for syntax.

optional.name: page
optional.description: Page number for results (1-indexed).

optional.name: sort
optional.description: Field to sort results by. If not specified, GitHub's 'best match' algorithm is used.

optional.name: order
optional.description: Sort order for results when `sort` is specified; ignored otherwise.

optional.name: per_page
optional.description: Number of search results per page. Maximum 100.

title: Set admin branch protection
description: Enables administrator enforcement on a branch, making existing protection rules also apply to administrators; branch protection rules must already be configured.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension. Not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (user or organization name). Not case sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: Branch name. Wildcards not permitted (use GitHub GraphQL API for wildcard patterns).

title: Set app access restrictions
description: Replaces the list of GitHub Apps permitted to push to a protected branch. This action completely replaces the existing list of apps with push access - it does not add to or merge with the current list. Requirements: - The branch must already have protection rules enabled with push restrictions configured - Apps must be installed on the repository and have 'contents' write permission - Push restrictions are only available for organization-owned repositories with GitHub Team or Enterprise Cloud plans

required.name: apps
required.description: The list of GitHub App slugs to grant push access. This replaces the entire list of apps with push access. Apps must be installed on the repository and have 'contents' write permission. The app slug is the URL-friendly name of the GitHub App (e.g., 'github-actions', 'dependabot').

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The organization or username that owns the repository. Push restrictions are only available for organization-owned repositories.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the protected branch. Wildcards are not permitted. The branch must already have protection rules enabled with push restrictions configured.

title: Set a repository subscription
description: Sets the authenticated user's notification subscription for a repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: ignored
optional.description: Determines if all notifications should be blocked from this repository. If `true`, this repository will be ignored, and the `subscribed` parameter will be disregarded (effectively setting subscribed to `false`).

optional.name: subscribed
optional.description: Determines if notifications should be received from this repository. Set to `true` to watch the repository, `false` to unwatch. This parameter is overridden if `ignored` is set to `true`.

title: Set a thread subscription
description: Sets whether a GitHub notification thread is ignored (muted) or unignored (unmuted), for a `thread_id` that must identify an existing notification thread.

required.name: thread_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the notification thread (e.g., from `GET /notifications`).

optional.name: ignored
optional.description: Whether to ignore (mute) the thread. `True` blocks notifications; `False` allows them if otherwise subscribed.

title: Set default workflow permissions for an organization
description: Updates an organization's default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions for workflows and whether GitHub Actions can approve pull requests; note that allowing Actions to approve pull requests (`can_approve_pull_request_reviews: true`) is a security risk.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: default_workflow_permissions
optional.description: Specifies the default permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN in GitHub Actions workflows.

optional.name: can_approve_pull_request_reviews
optional.description: Whether GitHub Actions can approve pull requests; enabling this (`true`) can be a security risk. If omitted, the current setting is preserved.

title: Set default workflow permissions for a repository
description: Sets the default permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN within a repository and configures whether GitHub Actions can approve pull requests.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.

optional.name: default_workflow_permissions
optional.description: The default permissions granted to the GITHUB_TOKEN when running workflows in the repository. 'read' allows read-only access, while 'write' allows write access.

optional.name: can_approve_pull_request_reviews
optional.description: Specifies whether GitHub Actions workflows, using the GITHUB_TOKEN, can approve pull requests. Enabling this can pose a security risk by allowing automated processes to approve code changes.

title: Set primary email visibility
description: Sets the visibility ('public' or 'private') of the authenticated user's primary email address on GitHub, if one is configured.

required.name: visibility
required.description: Desired visibility for the authenticated user's primary email. Use 'public' to make the email visible on the user's profile, or 'private' to hide it.

title: Set GitHub Actions permissions for an organization
description: Sets the GitHub Actions permissions policy for an organization, specifying which repositories can run Actions and which actions/workflows are allowed; if 'selected' is chosen for either, manage the specific lists via other endpoints.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name (not case-sensitive).

required.name: enabled_repositories
required.description: Policy for which repositories can run GitHub Actions. If 'selected', manage the list of specific repositories via other GitHub API endpoints.

optional.name: allowed_actions
optional.description: Policy for which actions and reusable workflows are allowed. If 'selected', manage the list of specific actions/workflows via other GitHub API endpoints. Required when enabled_repositories is set to 'all' or 'selected'.

optional.name: sha_pinning_required
optional.description: Whether actions and reusable workflows must be pinned to full-length commit SHAs. This enforces an additional security requirement for GitHub Actions.

title: Set github actions permissions for a repository
description: Sets GitHub Actions permissions for a repository, enabling/disabling Actions and defining the policy for allowed actions and reusable workflows.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: enabled
required.description: Specifies whether GitHub Actions is enabled for the repository. Set to `True` to enable, `False` to disable.

optional.name: allowed_actions
optional.description: Permissions policy: `all` (all actions/workflows allowed), `local_only` (only from this repository), or `selected` (configured in settings). Optional; inherits from organization/enterprise or GitHub defaults if omitted.

title: Set interaction restrictions for an organization
description: Limits interactions (comments, new issues, PRs) in an organization's public repositories by user type and duration, typically to mitigate high traffic or unwanted activity.

required.name: org
required.description: Name of the organization (case-insensitive).

required.name: limit
required.description: Type of GitHub user to be restricted from commenting, opening issues, or creating pull requests in the organization's public repositories.

optional.name: expiry
optional.description: Duration of the restriction; if omitted, the API defaults to `one_day`. A new limit overwrites any existing one.

title: Set interaction restrictions for a repository
description: Temporarily limits which GitHub users (e.g., existing_users, contributors_only) can interact (comment, open issues, create pull requests) in a repository for a specified duration.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository (without .git extension, case-insensitive).

required.name: limit
required.description: Specifies which group of GitHub users (e.g., existing_users, contributors_only) can interact with the repository.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (username or organization name, case-insensitive).

optional.name: expiry
optional.description: Duration for the interaction restriction (e.g., one_day, six_months); API defaults to 'one_day' if not provided.

title: Set interaction restrictions for your public repositories
description: Sets or updates temporary interaction restrictions for all public repositories owned by the authenticated user, overriding any repository-specific limits.

required.name: limit
required.description: Specifies the type of GitHub user that can comment, open issues, or create pull requests in your public repositories while the interaction limit is in effect.

optional.name: expiry
optional.description: Specifies the duration of the interaction restriction; API defaults to `one_day` if not provided.

title: Set labels for an issue
description: Replaces all existing labels on a GitHub issue with a new set of labels.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: labels
required.description: A list of label names to apply to the issue. This replaces all existing labels on the issue. Providing an empty list will remove all labels from the issue.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The number that identifies the issue within the repository.

title: Set custom OIDC subject claim template
description: Sets the OpenID Connect (OIDC) subject claim template for a GitHub repository, allowing use of the default template or a custom one defined by `include_claim_keys` if `use_default` is `false`.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Owner of the repository (username or organization name, case-insensitive).

required.name: use_default
required.description: If true, applies the default GitHub-provided OIDC subject claim template (ignoring `include_claim_keys`); if false, a custom template defined by `include_claim_keys` is used.

optional.name: include_claim_keys
optional.description: Array of unique OIDC claim strings (alphanumeric and underscores) for the token. Used only if `use_default` is `false`. Consult GitHub's OIDC documentation for supported claim keys.

title: Set allowed actions and workflows for an organization
description: Sets the GitHub Actions permissions for an existing organization, specifying allowed GitHub-owned actions, verified creator actions, and action/workflow patterns from public repositories.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: patterns_allowed
optional.description: String-matching patterns for allowed actions/workflows from public repositories (e.g., `monalisa/octocat@*`, `monalisa/*`); supports wildcards, tags, SHAs.

optional.name: verified_allowed
optional.description: Whether actions from GitHub Marketplace verified creators are allowed.

optional.name: github_owned_allowed
optional.description: Whether GitHub-owned actions (e.g., from the `actions` organization) are allowed.

title: Set custom labels for a self-hosted runner for an organization
description: Sets the custom labels for a self-hosted runner in an organization; this operation does not affect default system-assigned labels (e.g., 'self-hosted', 'linux', 'x64').

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: labels
required.description: A list of custom label names to set for the runner. This replaces all existing custom labels. Provide an empty list to remove all custom labels from the runner.

required.name: runner_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner.

title: Set repo allowed actions
description: Sets allowed GitHub Actions and reusable workflows for a repository, managing permissions for GitHub-owned, verified creator, or specific pattern-matched actions/workflows (note: `patterns_allowed` applies only to public repositories).

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: patterns_allowed
optional.description: String-matching patterns (wildcards, tags, SHAs allowed) for specific actions/workflows; **Note**: Only applies to public repositories.

optional.name: verified_allowed
optional.description: Determines if actions from GitHub Marketplace verified creators are allowed.

optional.name: github_owned_allowed
optional.description: Determines if GitHub-owned actions (e.g., from the `actions` organization) are allowed.

title: Set custom labels for repo runner
description: Replaces all custom labels for a specific self-hosted runner in a repository; an empty list for `labels` removes all existing custom labels.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

required.name: labels
required.description: Custom labels to set for the runner; an empty list removes all custom labels and replaces existing ones.

required.name: runner_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the self-hosted runner.

title: Set selected repositories for an organization variable
description: Replaces the list of repositories that can access an organization-level variable; the variable's visibility must be 'selected'.

required.name: org
required.description: The slug or name of the GitHub organization. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: name
required.description: The name of the organization variable for which to set repository access.

required.name: selected_repository_ids
required.description: A list of unique integer identifiers for the repositories that can access the organization variable. This list will replace any current selection of repositories. An empty list will remove access for all repositories.

title: Set selected repositories for an organization secret
description: Replaces the list of repositories that can access an organization secret; only effective if the secret's visibility is 'selected'. Prerequisites: - The organization secret must already exist - The secret's visibility must be set to 'selected' (not 'all' or 'private') - Requires admin:org scope or actions secrets fine-grained permission This action completely replaces the repository access list. To add or remove individual repositories without affecting others, use the dedicated add/remove repository actions instead.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the organization secret whose repository access list is being updated.

required.name: selected_repository_ids
required.description: An array of unique integer IDs for repositories that will be granted access to the organization secret. This completely replaces the existing list. Use dedicated actions to add or remove individual repositories without replacing the entire list.

title: Set selected repositories for a user secret
description: Defines the list of repositories permitted to access a specific Codespaces secret for the authenticated user.

required.name: secret_name
required.description: The name of the Codespaces secret for which to set repository access. This secret must already exist for the authenticated user.

required.name: selected_repository_ids
required.description: A list of repository IDs to which the secret will be granted access. This list completely replaces any existing set of repositories for the secret. Each repository ID must correspond to a repository accessible by the authenticated user.

title: Set status check contexts
description: Replaces required status check contexts for a protected branch, requiring admin permissions; an empty `contexts` array removes all checks.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension; not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner (username or organization) of the repository; not case sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch for which to set status check contexts; cannot contain wildcard characters.

required.name: contexts
required.description: Names of the status checks to require; an empty array removes all required status checks.

title: Set team access restrictions
description: Replaces the list of teams with push access to a protected branch. This action sets (replaces) the teams that have push access to a protected branch. Unlike 'Add team access restrictions' (POST), this action replaces the entire list rather than adding to it. Use an empty list to remove all team restrictions. Prerequisites: - The repository must be owned by an organization (not a personal account) - The branch must have protection rules enabled - The branch protection must have restrictions configured - The teams must exist in the organization and have repository access

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The organization name that owns the repository. Team access restrictions only work for organization-owned repositories, not personal repositories. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: teams
required.description: The list of team slugs to grant push access to the protected branch. A team slug is the URL-friendly version of the team name (lowercase, hyphens instead of spaces). The teams must already have access to the repository. This REPLACES the entire existing list of teams with push access (use empty list to remove all teams).

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the protected branch to set team restrictions on. The branch must already have branch protection enabled with restrictions configured. Wildcard characters are not supported. For wildcard branch protection, use the GitHub GraphQL API.

title: Set user access restrictions
description: Replaces the list of users with push access to a protected branch in an organization repository. Important notes: - This action only works on organization-owned repositories (not personal repos) - The branch must already have protection rules with restrictions enabled - This REPLACES (not adds to) the existing list of users with push access - Users must have write access to the repository to be added - The combined total of users, apps, and teams is limited to 100 items - To add users without replacing, use the 'add_user_access_restrictions' action instead

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository (must be an organization for user restrictions). This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: users
required.description: The list of user logins (usernames) to grant push access to the protected branch. This REPLACES the existing list of users. Users must have write access to the repository. Pass an empty list [] to remove all user restrictions. The combined total of users, apps, and teams is limited to 100 items.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch. Cannot contain wildcard characters. To use wildcards in branch names, use the GitHub GraphQL API.

title: Set User Interaction Limit (GraphQL)
description: Tool to set interaction limits on a user's public repositories using GraphQL. Use when you need to temporarily restrict who can comment, open issues, or create pull requests. Limits apply to the authenticated user or a specified user.

required.name: limit
required.description: The level of interaction to limit. EXISTING_USERS limits to users with accounts older than 24 hours, CONTRIBUTORS_ONLY limits to prior contributors, COLLABORATORS_ONLY limits to collaborators only.

required.name: user_id
required.description: The global ID of the user to set interaction limits for. This is required and must be a valid GitHub user node ID.

optional.name: expiry
optional.description: When the interaction limit expires.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. Used to track requests.

title: Set workflow access level outside repository
description: Sets the access level for workflows outside a repository to use actions and reusable workflows within that repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without `.git` extension. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Owner's username or organization name. Not case-sensitive.

required.name: access_level
required.description:
Specifies the level of access workflows outside this repository have to its actions and reusable workflows.
- `none`: Actions and reusable workflows are accessible only from workflows within this repository.
- `user`: Actions and reusable workflows can be shared with other private repositories owned by the same user.
- `organization`: Actions and reusable workflows can be shared with other repositories within the same organization.

title: Star a gist
description: Stars a GitHub gist identified by `gist_id`; this action is idempotent and returns a 204 No Content status upon success, even if the gist is already starred.

required.name: gist_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the gist. This ID is the string of characters found at the end of a gist's URL.

title: Star a specified repository (requires owner and repo)
description: Stars a specified repository (identified by owner and repo name) for the authenticated user; this action is idempotent and succeeds even if the repository is already starred. Requires explicit repository identification via owner and repo parameters.

required.name: repo
required.description: Required. The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Required. The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

title: Start a codespace for the authenticated user
description: Initiates the startup process for an existing GitHub Codespace (identified by `codespace_name`) if it's in a startable state like 'Available' or 'Stopped'.

required.name: codespace_name
required.description: The unique name of the codespace to be started. This is the identifier for the codespace, often system-generated or user-defined.

title: Stop a codespace for an organization user
description: Stops a running codespace for an organization member. This action allows organization administrators to stop a codespace that belongs to a member of their organization. The codespace must be in a running state (e.g., 'Available') to be stopped. Required permissions: - OAuth/PAT: admin:org scope - Fine-grained tokens: 'Organization codespaces' (write) or 'Codespaces lifecycle admin' (write) Common HTTP responses: - 200: Codespace successfully stopped, returns codespace object - 304: Not modified (codespace already stopped) - 401: Authentication required - 403: Insufficient permissions (need admin:org) - 404: Organization, user, or codespace not found

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name (login). Case-insensitive. The authenticated user must have admin:org permissions for this organization.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username (login) of the organization member whose codespace will be stopped.

required.name: codespace_name
required.description: The unique name of the codespace to stop. This is typically a hyphenated string like 'username-repo-name-randomchars'. You can obtain this from the 'List codespaces for a user in organization' action.

title: Stop a codespace for the authenticated user
description: Stops a running or available Codespace for the authenticated user, pausing its execution and billing.

required.name: codespace_name
required.description: The unique name of the Codespace to be stopped. This name is assigned by GitHub when the Codespace is created.

title: Submit a review for a pull request
description: Finalizes a pending pull request review (identified by `review_id`) with a required `event` (APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, COMMENT) and an optional `body`.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Case-insensitive.

required.name: event
required.description: The review action: `APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, or `COMMENT`. An invalid/omitted event will result in an HTTP 422 error and set the review state to `PENDING`, requiring a subsequent valid submission.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. Case-insensitive.

required.name: review_id
required.description: Identifier of the pending review to be submitted. Typically obtained when a review is first created or initiated.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: The number that uniquely identifies the pull request.

optional.name: body
optional.description: The main textual content of the review. Highly recommended for `COMMENT` events to provide context; can also supplement `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES` actions.

title: Sync a fork branch with the upstream repository
description: Synchronizes a branch in a forked GitHub repository with its upstream counterpart, assuming the repository is a fork, the branch exists, an upstream is configured, and the merge is conflict-free.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the forked repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username or organization name of the account that owns the forked repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch
required.description: The name of the branch in the forked repository that should be updated to match the corresponding branch in the upstream repository.

title: Test the push repository webhook
description: Triggers a simulated push event to test a repository's push webhook; a test event is only delivered if the webhook is subscribed to 'push' events, otherwise, it returns 204 No Content without sending a POST.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

required.name: hook_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the hook, found in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery or by listing repository webhooks.

title: Transfer a repository
description: Initiates a repository transfer to a new owner (who must accept the request); if the new owner is an organization, it must be configured to allow transfers.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository to transfer, without `.git` (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Current owner's username or organization name (case-insensitive).

required.name: new_owner
required.description: Target username or organization name for the repository transfer.

optional.name: new_name
optional.description: Optional new name for the repository post-transfer; retains current name if unspecified.

optional.name: team_ids
optional.description: List of team IDs to add the repository to if `new_owner` is an organization; teams must belong to the `new_owner`.

title: Unblock a user
description: Unblocks a GitHub user, provided they are currently blocked by the authenticated user.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username (handle) of the user to unblock.

title: Unblock a user from an organization
description: Unblocks a user from an organization, allowing renewed interaction with its resources, provided the user is currently blocked (otherwise, a 404 error may occur).

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This is case-insensitive.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username of the user to unblock.

title: Unfollow a user
description: Unfollows an existing GitHub user; this action is idempotent, succeeding even if the authenticated user is not currently following them.

required.name: username
required.description: The GitHub username (handle) of the user whom the authenticated user wishes to unfollow.

title: Unfollow organization
description: Tool to unfollow a GitHub organization using GraphQL. Use when you need to stop following a specific organization on GitHub.

required.name: organization_id
required.description: The Node ID of the organization to unfollow (e.g., 'MDEyOk9yZ2FuaXphdGlvbjk5MTk='). This is the global GraphQL node ID, not the organization name or numeric ID.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. This value will be returned in the response and can be used for request tracking or idempotency.

title: Unfollow user
description: Tool to unfollow a GitHub user using GraphQL. Use when you need to stop following a specific user on GitHub.

required.name: user_id
required.description: The Node ID of the user to unfollow (e.g., 'MDQ6VXNlcjE='). This is the global GraphQL node ID, not the username or numeric user ID.

optional.name: client_mutation_id
optional.description: A unique identifier for the client performing the mutation. This value will be returned in the response and can be used for request tracking or idempotency.

title: Unlock an issue
description: Unlocks a currently locked GitHub issue in the specified repository, allowing new comments and interactions.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username (account) or organization name that owns the repository. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: issue_number
required.description: The number that uniquely identifies the issue within the repository.

title: Unlock an organization repository
description: Unlocks a repository that was locked for migration within a GitHub organization. This action is part of the organization migrations workflow. When you start a migration with `lock_repositories=true`, the source repositories are locked to prevent changes during export. After the migration is complete and applied to the target instance, use this action to unlock the repositories so they can be accessed or deleted. Requirements: - You must be an organization owner to unlock repositories - The repository must be currently locked as part of the specified migration - This endpoint does not work with GitHub App tokens or fine-grained personal access tokens Typical workflow: 1. Start an organization migration with POST /orgs/{org}/migrations 2. Wait for the migration to complete (state: "exported") 3. Apply the migration to your target instance 4. Unlock each migrated repository using this action 5. Delete the source repositories if no longer needed

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the GitHub organization that owns the migration. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: repo_name
required.description: The name of the repository to unlock. Must be one of the repositories included in the specified migration.

required.name: migration_id
required.description: The unique numeric identifier of the organization migration. You can find this by listing organization migrations using GET /orgs/{org}/migrations.

title: Unlock a user repository
description: Unlocks a repository (`repo_name`) that was locked as part of a user migration (`migration_id`), making it usable or deletable; this action requires the repository to be currently locked.

required.name: repo_name
required.description: The name of the repository to unlock.

required.name: migration_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the user migration.

title: Unstar a gist
description: Removes a star from the specified gist; the action is idempotent and will not error if the gist was not previously starred by the user.

required.name: gist_id
required.description: The unique identifier (ID) of the gist to be unstarred. This ID can be retrieved from API endpoints that list gists or from the gist's URL.

title: Unstar a repository
description: Removes the authenticated user's star from a specified repository, which must already be starred by the user.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the repository owner (case-insensitive).

title: Update a check run
description: Updates an existing check run for a specific commit in a repository, allowing modifications to its status, conclusion, output, and other details. NOTE: This endpoint requires GitHub App authentication with 'checks:write' permission - OAuth tokens and personal access tokens cannot update check runs.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name without the `.git` extension (not case sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (not case sensitive).

required.name: check_run_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the check run.

optional.name: name
optional.description: Name of the check (e.g., "code-coverage").

optional.name: status
optional.description: Current status of the check run. Only GitHub Actions can set `waiting`, `pending`, or `requested`.

optional.name: actions
optional.description: JSON string representing user-triggerable actions (max 3), each with `label`, `identifier`, and `description`.

optional.name: conclusion
optional.description: Final conclusion of the check. Required if `completed_at` is provided or `status` is `completed`. Providing `conclusion` sets `status` to `completed`. Users cannot set `stale`.

optional.name: started_at
optional.description: Timestamp of when the check run started (ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).

optional.name: details_url
optional.description: URL of the integrator's site with full check details.

optional.name: external_id
optional.description: Reference for the run on the integrator's system.

optional.name: completed_at
optional.description: Timestamp of when the check run completed (ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).

optional.name: output_text
optional.description: Text for the output, can contain Markdown.

optional.name: output_title
optional.description: Title for the check run output. Displayed prominently in the GitHub checks UI.

optional.name: output_images
optional.description: JSON string representing images for the output, displayed in the GitHub PR UI.

optional.name: output_summary
optional.description: Summary of the output, can contain Markdown. Required if the `output` object is provided.

optional.name: output_annotations
optional.description: JSON string representing line-specific analysis information, visible in PRs. Max 50 per request (appended to existing). GitHub Actions: 10 warnings/10 errors per step.

title: Update a code scanning alert
description: Updates a specific code scanning alert in a GitHub repository, primarily to change its state (e.g., 'open' or 'dismissed').

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: state
required.description: The new state for the code scanning alert. Must be either 'open' or 'dismissed'. If 'dismissed', `dismissed_reason` is mandatory.

required.name: alert_number
required.description: The number that identifies an alert. Found in the alert's URL or the `number` field of the GET alerts API response.

optional.name: dismissed_reason
optional.description: The reason for dismissing or closing the alert. **Required if `state` is 'dismissed'.**

optional.name: dismissed_comment
optional.description: An optional comment to provide further context when dismissing an alert. Maximum 280 characters.

title: Update a commit comment
description: Changes the body of an existing commit comment.

required.name: body
required.description: The new content of the comment.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: comment_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the comment.

title: Update a custom organization role
description: Updates an existing custom role in an organization by modifying its name, description, or permissions; at least one of these fields must be provided.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name (not case-sensitive).

required.name: role_id
required.description: Unique identifier of the custom organization role.

optional.name: name
optional.description: New name for the custom role. Unchanged if omitted.

optional.name: base_role
optional.description: The system role from which this role inherits permissions. One of: 'none', 'read', 'triage', 'write', 'maintain', or 'admin'. Unchanged if omitted.

optional.name: description
optional.description: New short description for the role. Unchanged if omitted.

optional.name: permissions
optional.description: New list of GitHub organization permissions for the role, replacing existing ones. An empty list removes all permissions. Unchanged if omitted.

title: Update a deployment branch policy
description: Updates the name pattern of an existing deployment branch policy for a specific environment in a repository.

required.name: name
required.description: The new name pattern that branches must match to deploy to this environment. Wildcard characters (`*`) can be used but will not match `/`. For example, to match branches that begin with `release/` and contain an additional single slash, use `release/*/*`. For more information about pattern matching syntax, refer to the Ruby File.fnmatch documentation (https://ruby-doc.org/core-2.5.1/File.html#method-c-fnmatch).

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: branch_policy_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the deployment branch policy to be updated.

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the deployment environment. This name must be URL-encoded if it contains special characters such as slashes (e.g., replace `/` with `%2F`).

title: Update a discussion
description: Updates the title and/or body of a specific team discussion within an organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name (not case-sensitive).

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name.

required.name: discussion_number
required.description: The unique number that identifies the discussion within the team.

optional.name: body
optional.description: The new body text for the discussion post. Supports markdown formatting. Only provide this if you want to change the body content.

optional.name: title
optional.description: The new title for the discussion post. Only provide this if you want to change the title.

title: Update a discussion comment
description: Updates the body of a comment in a team's discussion within an organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This is not case sensitive.

required.name: body
required.description: The new body text for the discussion comment. Supports GitHub Flavored Markdown.

required.name: team_slug
required.description: The slug of the team name. This is the team name converted to lowercase with spaces replaced by hyphens (e.g., 'justice-league').

required.name: comment_number
required.description: The unique number identifying the comment within the discussion.

required.name: discussion_number
required.description: The unique number identifying the discussion.

title: Update a gist
description: Updates a gist's description, and/or its files (including content, filename changes, or deletion).

required.name: gist_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the gist to be updated.

optional.name: files
optional.description: Specifies changes to gist files as a JSON string. Keys are current filenames (e.g., `hello.py`). For each file: update `content`, assign a new `filename` to rename (or both). To delete a file, set its value to `null` or an object without `content` or `filename`. Files not mentioned are preserved.

optional.name: description
optional.description: A new description for the gist.

title: Update a gist comment
description: Updates an existing comment on a specified gist.

required.name: body
required.description: The new text content for the comment. Supports Markdown formatting.

required.name: gist_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the gist. This is typically a 32-character hexadecimal string found in the gist URL.

required.name: comment_id
required.description: The unique numeric identifier of the comment to update.

title: Update a label
description: Updates an existing label's name, color, or description within a specified repository.

required.name: name
required.description: Current name of the label to be updated; value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the .git extension; value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository; value is not case-sensitive.

optional.name: color
optional.description: Hexadecimal color code for the label, without the leading '#' (e.g., 'f29513').

optional.name: new_name
optional.description: New name for the label (not case-sensitive). Emoji can be added using native characters or colon-style markup (e.g., ':strawberry:'). Refer to GitHub's emoji cheat sheet for a full list of codes.

optional.name: description
optional.description: Short description for the label (max 100 characters).

title: Update a milestone
description: Updates a milestone in a repository, identified by `owner`, `repo`, and `milestone_number`, by allowing modification of its `title`, `state`, `description`, or `due_on`; at least one of these four attributes must be provided to perform an update.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The username of the account that owns the repository. This field is not case-sensitive.

required.name: milestone_number
required.description: The unique number that identifies the milestone.

optional.name: state
optional.description: The new state of the milestone. If not provided, the state will remain unchanged. Defaults to 'open'.

optional.name: title
optional.description: The new title for the milestone. If not provided, the title will remain unchanged.

optional.name: due_on
optional.description: The milestone due date in ISO 8601 format: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. If not provided, the due date will remain unchanged. To remove the due date, pass an empty string or `null`.

optional.name: description
optional.description: A new description for the milestone. If not provided, the description will remain unchanged.

title: Update an environment variable
description: Updates an existing environment variable's name and/or value in a specific GitHub repository environment; requires providing either a new name or a new value.

required.name: name
required.description: Current name of the environment variable to update.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository without the `.git` extension. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: environment_name
required.description: The name of the environment. The name must be URL encoded (e.g., replace slashes `/` with `%2F`).

optional.name: value
optional.description: New value for the environment variable; if omitted, the value is not changed.

optional.name: new_name
optional.description: New name for the environment variable. If provided, the variable will be renamed to this value. If omitted, the name remains unchanged.

title: Update an issue
description: Updates an existing GitHub issue's title, body, state, milestone, labels, or assignees; `state_reason` is only processed if `state` also changes, and use `null` or `[]` to clear applicable fields.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

required.name: issue_number
required.description: Unique number identifying the issue.

optional.name: body
optional.description: New issue body; send `null` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.

optional.name: state
optional.description: New issue state; omit to leave unchanged.

optional.name: title
optional.description: New issue title; send `null` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.

optional.name: labels
optional.description: Replaces all existing labels. Send `[]` to remove all; omit to leave unchanged. Requires push access for changes.

optional.name: assignee
optional.description: DEPRECATED: Username to assign; use `assignees`. Send `null` to unassign, omit to leave unchanged.

optional.name: assignees
optional.description: Replaces all existing assignees. Send `[]` to remove all; omit to leave unchanged. Requires push access for changes.

optional.name: milestone
optional.description: Milestone ID (as string) or title. Send `null` to clear; omit to leave unchanged. Numeric ID recommended.

optional.name: state_reason
optional.description: Reason for state change, considered only if `state` also changes. Valid reasons depend on the new `state`.

title: Update an issue comment
description: Updates an existing comment on an issue or pull request within a specified repository. You can only update comments that the authenticated user has permission to edit. The comment_id can be obtained from the list_issue_comments or get_an_issue_comment actions.

required.name: body
required.description: New content for the issue comment (GitHub Flavored Markdown supported).

required.name: repo
required.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Username of the account owning the repository (not case-sensitive).

required.name: comment_id
required.description: Unique ID of the issue comment to update.

title: Update an organization
description: Updates an organization's settings; changing security-related fields requires admin, owner, or security manager permissions.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization's unique, case-insensitive identifier.

optional.name: blog
optional.description: URL of the organization's blog.

optional.name: name
optional.description: Display name.

optional.name: email
optional.description: Publicly visible email address.

optional.name: company
optional.description: Company name.

optional.name: location
optional.description: Geographical location.

optional.name: description
optional.description: Short description.

optional.name: billing_email
optional.description: Billing email address (not publicly visible).

optional.name: twitter_username
optional.description: Twitter username.

optional.name: has_repository_projects
optional.description: Whether repository-level projects can be used within the organization.

optional.name: members_can_create_pages
optional.description: Whether members can create GitHub Pages sites. Does not affect existing sites.

optional.name: has_organization_projects
optional.description: Whether organization-level projects can be used.

optional.name: web_commit_signoff_required
optional.description: Whether web interface commits require sign-off.

optional.name: default_repository_permission
optional.description: Default permission for members on organization repositories.

optional.name: members_can_create_public_pages
optional.description: Whether members can create public GitHub Pages sites. Does not affect existing sites.

optional.name: members_can_create_repositories
optional.description: Whether non-admin members can create repositories. Overridden by `members_allowed_repository_creation_type`.

optional.name: members_can_create_private_pages
optional.description: Whether members can create private GitHub Pages sites. Does not affect existing sites.

optional.name: members_can_fork_private_repositories
optional.description: Whether members can fork private repositories of the organization.

optional.name: members_can_create_public_repositories
optional.description: Whether members can create public repositories.

optional.name: members_can_create_private_repositories
optional.description: Whether members can create private repositories.

optional.name: members_allowed_repository_creation_type
optional.description: Types of repositories non-admin members can create. `private` option only on GitHub Enterprise Cloud. Deprecated; overrides `members_can_create_repositories`.

optional.name: members_can_create_internal_repositories
optional.description: Whether members can create internal repositories. Only for organizations in an enterprise account.

optional.name: secret_scanning_push_protection_custom_link
optional.description: URL displayed if `secret_scanning_push_protection_custom_link_enabled` is true and a push is blocked.

optional.name: secret_scanning_enabled_for_new_repositories
optional.description: Automatically enable secret scanning for new repositories.

optional.name: dependency_graph_enabled_for_new_repositories
optional.description: Automatically enable dependency graph for new repositories.

optional.name: advanced_security_enabled_for_new_repositories
optional.description: Automatically enable GitHub Advanced Security for new repositories.

optional.name: dependabot_alerts_enabled_for_new_repositories
optional.description: Automatically enable Dependabot alerts for new repositories.

optional.name: secret_scanning_push_protection_custom_link_enabled
optional.description: Show custom link to contributors blocked by secret scanning push protection.

optional.name: dependabot_security_updates_enabled_for_new_repositories
optional.description: Automatically enable Dependabot security updates for new repositories.

optional.name: secret_scanning_push_protection_enabled_for_new_repositories
optional.description: Automatically enable secret scanning push protection for new repositories.

title: Update an organization variable
description: Updates an existing GitHub Actions organization variable's name, value, or visibility (`all`, `private`, `selected`), requiring `selected_repository_ids` with valid repository IDs if visibility is `selected`.

required.name: org
required.description: The organization name. The name is not case sensitive.

required.name: name
required.description: The current name of the organization variable to be updated. This name is case-sensitive.

optional.name: value
optional.description: Optional: The new value for the organization variable. If provided, the variable's value will be updated. If omitted or null, the current value is preserved.

optional.name: new_name
optional.description: Optional: The new name for the organization variable. If provided, the variable will be renamed. If omitted or null, the current name is preserved.

optional.name: visibility
optional.description: Optional: Specifies the new visibility of the organization variable. Determines which repositories can access this variable: 'all' (all repositories), 'private' (only private repositories), or 'selected' (specific repositories). When set to 'selected', you must also provide `selected_repository_ids`. If omitted or null, visibility remains unchanged.

optional.name: selected_repository_ids
optional.description: Optional: A list of repository IDs (integers) that can access this organization variable. Required when `visibility` is set to 'selected'. Ignored for other visibility values. If omitted when visibility='selected', the API may reject the request or use existing repository access list.

title: Update an organization webhook
description: Updates the configuration (URL, content type, secret, SSL verification), subscribed events, active status, or name of an existing webhook for a specified organization.

required.name: org
required.description: The name of the organization. This value is not case-sensitive.

required.name: hook_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the webhook. This ID can be found in the `X-GitHub-Hook-ID` header of a webhook delivery.

optional.name: name
optional.description: Must be passed as 'web' for organization webhooks. This is a fixed value required by the GitHub API.

optional.name: active
optional.description: Set to `true` to send notifications, or `false` to disable them.

optional.name: events
optional.description: List of events that trigger this webhook. GitHub REPLACES the full event list when this is sent — omit (leave unset) to preserve the existing event subscription. Use `['*']` to subscribe to all events. See GitHub docs for available event types.

optional.name: config_url
optional.description: Target URL for webhook payloads. Required if updating other `config` properties (e.g., `content_type`, `secret`), as GitHub mandates `url` when `config` is modified.

optional.name: config_secret
optional.description: Secret key for HMAC digest to ensure payload integrity. Refer to GitHub documentation on delivery headers for details.

optional.name: config_content_type
optional.description: Media type for serializing payloads (`json` or `form`). The API defaults to `form` if this field is not provided.

optional.name: config_insecure_ssl
optional.description: Controls SSL certificate verification for payload delivery. Set to '1' to skip verification (insecure), or '0' to enforce (API default). Use with caution.

title: Update a project
description: Updates an existing GitHub project (V2) attributes like title, description, visibility, and state. Note: This action uses GitHub's Projects V2 GraphQL API. The legacy Projects (classic) REST API was sunset on April 1, 2025. The project is identified by its number (visible in the project URL) and owner (either a username or organization name). If no owner is specified, the authenticated user is assumed. At least one field to update must be provided.

required.name: project_number
required.description: The project's sequential number (e.g., 1, 2, 3). This is displayed in the project URL as https://github.com/users/{username}/projects/{project_number}.

optional.name: org
optional.description: The organization that owns the project. If provided, this takes precedence over username.

optional.name: title
optional.description: The new title for the project. If not provided, the title will not be changed.

optional.name: closed
optional.description: Sets whether the project is closed. `True` closes the project, `False` reopens it. If not provided, the state will not be changed.

optional.name: public
optional.description: Sets the visibility of the project. `True` makes it public (visible to everyone), `False` makes it private. If not provided, the visibility will not be changed.

optional.name: readme
optional.description: The project's README content (supports Markdown formatting). If not provided, the README will not be changed.

optional.name: username
optional.description: The GitHub username who owns the project. If not provided, defaults to the authenticated user.

optional.name: short_description
optional.description: A short description for the project (displayed in project cards and listings). If not provided, the description will not be changed.

title: Update a pull request
description: Updates an existing pull request, allowing changes to attributes like title, body, state, base branch, and maintainer modification settings.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: pull_number
required.description: The unique number that identifies the pull request within the repository.

optional.name: base
optional.description: The name of the branch to which you want your changes pulled. This must be an existing branch in the current repository. Cannot update the base branch to point to another repository. If None, the base branch remains unchanged.

optional.name: body
optional.description: The new contents of the pull request. To remove the body, pass an empty string. If None, the body remains unchanged.

optional.name: state
optional.description: The new state of the pull request. Can be 'open' or 'closed'. If None, the state remains unchanged.

optional.name: title
optional.description: The new title for the pull request. If None, the title remains unchanged.

optional.name: maintainer_can_modify
optional.description: Indicates whether [maintainers can modify](https://docs.github.com/articles/allowing-changes-to-a-pull-request-branch-created-from-a-fork/) the pull request. If None, this setting remains unchanged.

title: Update a pull request branch
description: Updates an open pull request's head branch by merging the latest changes from its base branch, if mergeable and repository merging is enabled; operates asynchronously.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, without the `.git` extension (not case-sensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (not case-sensitive).

required.name: pull_number
required.description: Unique number identifying the pull request.

optional.name: expected_head_sha
optional.description: SHA of the expected head commit of the pull request's branch. If this SHA does not match the actual head SHA, the request fails (422 error), ensuring the branch was not updated unexpectedly. If omitted, the API uses the current head SHA of the branch.

title: Update a reference
description: Updates an existing Git reference (e.g., a branch or tag) to point to a specific commit SHA. By default, only allows fast-forward updates (where the new commit is a descendant of the current one). Set `force=true` to allow non-fast-forward updates that rewrite history. IMPORTANT: The reference must already exist - use 'Create a reference' action to create new refs.

required.name: ref
required.description: The name of the Git reference to update WITHOUT the 'refs/' prefix. For branches: use 'heads/<branch-name>' (e.g., 'heads/main', 'heads/feature-branch'). For tags: use 'tags/<tag-name>' (e.g., 'tags/v1.0.0'). Note: Branch references require 'heads/' (plural), not 'head/' (singular). Bare branch names will be automatically prefixed with 'heads/'. The reference must already exist - this endpoint only updates existing refs.

required.name: sha
required.description: The SHA1 commit hash to point this reference to. Must be exactly 40 hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f) representing a valid commit that exists in the repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: Repository name, excluding `.git` extension (case-insensitive).

required.name: owner
required.description: Account owner of the repository (case-insensitive).

optional.name: force
optional.description: Controls whether to allow non-fast-forward updates. When `false` (default), the new commit must be a direct descendant of the current commit (fast-forward only) - this prevents accidental history rewriting. When `true`, allows moving the reference to any commit, even if it means rewriting history or moving backward. Set to `true` only when you need to force-push changes, reset a branch, or intentionally rewrite commit history.

title: Update a release
description: Updates an existing release in a GitHub repository, allowing modification of its attributes; if linking a discussion, the `discussion_category_name` must refer to an existing category in the repository.

required.name: repo
required.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: owner
required.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

required.name: release_id
required.description: The unique identifier of the release to be updated.

optional.name: body
optional.description: Text describing the contents of the release. Supports GitHub Flavored Markdown.

optional.name: name
optional.description: The title of the release.

optional.name: draft
optional.description: Set to `true` to mark the release as a draft, or `false` to publish it. Default: `false`.

optional.name: tag_name
optional.description: The name of the tag. This can be an existing tag or a new tag name.

optional.name: prerelease
optional.description: Set to `true` to identify the release as a pre-release, or `false` for a full release. Default: `false`.

optional.name: make_latest
optional.description: Specifies whether this release should be set as the latest release for the repository. Accepts 'true', 'false', or 'legacy'. Drafts and pre-releases cannot be set as latest. Defaults to `true` for newly published releases. `legacy` specifies that the latest release should be determined based on the release creation date and higher semantic version.

optional.name: target_commitish
optional.description: Specifies the commitish value (e.g., branch name or commit SHA) that determines where the Git tag is created from. Can be any branch or commit SHA. This parameter is unused if the Git tag specified by `tag_name` already exists. Defaults to the repository's default branch if omitted.

optional.name: discussion_category_name
optional.description: If specified, a discussion of this category is created and linked to the release. The category must already exist in the repository. This parameter is ignored if a discussion is already linked to the release. For more information, see "[Managing categories for discussions in your repository](https://docs.github.com/discussions/managing-discussions-for-your-community/managing-categories-for-discussions-in-your-repository)."

title: Update a release asset
description: Updates the name, label, or state of a release asset in a GitHub repository, requiring at least one of these properties to be provided for modification.
